items.statement: Next fiscal revenue target INR700-750 crores with PAT INR44-45 crores.
items.value: INR700-750 crores revenue, INR44-45 crores PAT
items.quote: I think next year INR700 crores, INR750 crores seems to be a very achievable kind of revenue figures with INR44 crores, INR45 crores PAT.

items.statement: Expects 35%+ CAGR over 3-4 years.
items.quote: For a 3 to 4 -year outlook, I think the company will consistently provide a CAGR of around 35% plus year-on-year basis.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guidance 35-45%.
items.quote: If I'm giving a guidance of INR750 crores, I am giving a guidance of 35% to 45%. So we will be meeting that guidance.

items.statement: FY25 PAT projected INR35-36 crores.
items.quote: I think INR 35 crores, INR36 crores is what we are projecting this year and INR44 crores to INR45 crores for next year.

items.statement: Bottom line growth expected 25-30%.
items.quote: And the bottom line, let's say, if this year is INR35 crores to INR36 crores, it will again continue by around 30% or so -- 25% to 30% so.

items.statement: No capex planned for next couple of years due to high gold prices.
items.quote: Next couple of years or at least 1 calendar year, we are not thinking of building up anything just because of a strong increase in gold prices.

items.statement: Order book around 65 kgs as of February end.
items.quote: Order book right now will be around 65 kgs. That is still the month of February end.

items.statement: Aims to sustain margins and grow top line.
items.quote: Looking forward, we would want to sustain our margins and we will want to grow the top line, let's say, in the next coming fiscal to INR700 crores, INR750 crores.

items.statement: Gold prices increased 10-15% in quarter.
items.quote: And yes, there is a current capacity is around 1 ,700 kg or 1 ,800 kg is already there in wholesale. So there is -- because of the price which has hiked up in this year also it has -- in this quarter, there is a hype around 10% to 15% from 75,000 to 88,000.

items.statement: Demand is strong in organized segment.
items.quote: The demand is strong. And the demand we are into an organized segment of doing retail or job work or wholesale.

items.statement: Revenue mix expected to remain 50-50 between B2C and B2B.
items.quote: Revenue mix, yes, it will be 50-50 as of this calendar year or the coming financial year, yes, the revenue mix will be again 50-50.

items.statement: High gold prices may affect volume guidance.
items.quote: But we are not able to meet our volume guidance because of the very high growth in terms of gold prices.

items.statement: Plans to increase working capital loan by INR50-70 crores.
items.quote: INR50 crores to INR70 crores minimum to increase from the existing collateral that we have taken out from the long term -- in which long-term loan was.

items.statement: ROE target 20-25% sustainable.
items.quote: 20% to 25% is the sustainable ROE, and we have always been -- throughout the business journey, the ROC or ROE is 20% to 25%.

items.statement: Retail revenue growth expected 40-45% next fiscal.
items.quote: So next year, you will be again seeing retail revenue growth to go up by 40% to 45%.

items.statement: Expects higher double-digit ARR growth in FY26, possibly mid-teens, ahead of 15%.
items.quote: Yes, we can say that, yes . At the end of the year with FY 26, end of the year, we can expect higher double-digit growth and possibly in the higher mid -teens. Definitely ahead of 15.

items.statement: Next year's CAPEX expected in range of Rs. 150 to 170 crore.
items.quote: Last quarter, the CAPEX plan is approximately Rs. 30 crore. And the next financial year, of various projects, the CAPEX should be in the range of Rs. 150 to Rs. 170 crore.

items.statement: PBT expected in range of Rs. 100 to 120 crore.
items.quote: Firstly, in terms of profitability, we do remain committed, since Rs. 60 crore of the interest liability has gone. So PBT will be in range of Rs. 100 crore to Rs. 120 crore.

items.statement: Plans to double key count to 5,048 keys over next five years.
items.quote: As of now, we operate 36 hotels with a total of 2,495 keys. Over the next five years, we are on track to double our key count to a total of 5,048 keys.

items.statement: Sale of 100 service apartments to add Rs. 100 crore annually for next 3 years.
items.quote: The sale of 100 service apartments will begin before the festive season this year and we will add close to Rs. 100 crore to our balance sheet every year for the next 3 years.

items.statement: Flurys margins expected in range of 18% to 20%, possibly exceeding.
items.quote: And the margins continue to be industry leading for us in the range of 18% to 20%. They have been like this, and we will possibly even exceed thes e percentages as we go forward.

items.statement: Plans to reach 200 Flurys stores by 2027 centenary year.
items.quote: Flurys, as you know, started in Calcutta in 1927, and we plan to reach 200 stores in 2027, its centenary year for Flurys.

items.statement: Expects 150 Flurys outlets matured by FY27.
items.quote: So, maturity of the outlets, I would say that in ‘26, ‘27 should be at least 150 outlets should have matured .

items.statement: Plans to add 30-50 Flurys outlets over next 2 years.
items.quote: And starting next year, over the next 2 years, we plan to add 30 - 50 outlets.

items.statement: Plans to add roughly 300 managed keys every year.
items.quote: Lastly, for each year, as far as the management contracts is concerned, we plan to add roughly about 300 keys every year.

items.statement: Expects palace hotels occupancy to stabilize at 40-50% in FY26-27.
items.quote: And as we go forward, these are going to stabilize in the range of 40% to 50% in FY26-27.

items.statement: Expects Chettinad palace ARR Rs. 15,000 and Patiala Rs. 45,000-50,000 next year.
items.quote: I am talking about YTD ARRs for the hotel in Chettinad to be in the range of Rs. 15,000 and for the Ran Bass Palace to be in the range of Rs. 45,000 to Rs. 50,000 in the coming year.

items.statement: Plans to open 200-room Pune hotel in April 2027 and 100-room Vizag in October 2027.
items.quote: So, in FY27, the hotels will open, the first hotel Pune is going to open in April 27 followed by Vizag 100 rooms in October of ‘27.

items.statement: Plans to open 250-room Kolkata EM Bypass hotel in April 2028.
items.quote: This project actually opens in April of 2028. So, in ‘28-29, you can expect 250 keys opening on account of our hotel in Calcutta.

items.statement: Plans to open 400 keys in Navi Mumbai and Jaipur in FY29.
items.quote: And along with that, in ‘29, we will open about 400 keys, which is Navi Mumbai and our hotel in Jaipur.

items.statement: Plans to add 170 rooms in Navi Mumbai, total 250 keys.
items.quote: So, we plan to add another 170 rooms for which we have already completed the schematic design drawings. They are actually being completed and we are now going to be shortly going for the sanction of these drawings and for the additional approval of FSI .

items.statement: Expects 15% revenue CAGR over next 2-3 years including new hospitals and existing productivity.
items.quote: So for the revenue, we -- like we said earlier, we expect a 15% kind of CAGR growth over the next 2 to 3 years, which includes the new hospitals also coming and also existing hospitals productivity improving.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected around 22% to 23%.
items.quote: At the margin level, at EBITDA level, we would be around the 22% to 23% mark. Given the size of the existing hospitals and the improvement in productivity there, we should be able to absorb the initial losses from the new hospitals.

items.statement: Raipur hospital 152 beds, INR55 crore investment, asset-light rental model, commences early April.
items.quote: ILS Hospital Raipur, a 152-bed facility is expected to commence operations in early April. With a INR55 crore investment and an asset -light rental -based model, the hospital features ICUs, HDUs, OTs and specializes in oncology care as well.

items.statement: Signed MOU for third hospital in Jamshedpur, 150 beds, estimated outlay INR65 crores.
items.quote: Additionally, we have signed an MOU for our third hospital in Jamshedpur, which will have a capacity of 150 beds and an est imated outlay of approximately INR65 crores.

items.statement: Aims to become 1,000-bed hospital chain within next 2 to 3 years.
items.quote: As previously announced, we are steadfast to become a 1,000 -bed hospital chain within the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Steadfast on 1,000 bed target by FY27; Raipur adds ~160 beds, Jamshedpur hopeful by Oct 2026.
items.quote: So we are still steadfast on the 1,000 bed challenge by FY '27, and we have taken significant steps to end up achieving that target. As disclosed earlier, the Raipur Hospital will be commencing, which will add around 160 -odd beds to our already 550 beds, taking a total almost 710 beds.

items.statement: Hopeful of commissioning Jamshedpur hospital by October 2026.
items.quote: We are hopeful of commissioning that hospital by October of 2026. Apart from that, we are also evaluating certain acquisition opportunities for ongoing hospitals, which when they click, will definitely add to the bed capacity much faster than that.

items.statement: Jamshedpur project should be operational by FY26 because it is under construction.
items.quote: But as a second safeguard, we have onboarded the Jamshedpur project in the state of Jharkhand, which should be operational by FY '26 because it is already an under construction building.

items.statement: Looking to stabilize ARPOB increase around 7%, 8% annually through newer treatments and insurance rate differentiation.
items.quote: The ARPOB has increased at a healthy rate across all our hospitals. We are looking at stabilizing the ARPOB increase in the next -- to around the 7%, 8% mark on a annual basis. This will be through newer treatments and through the rate differentiation of the insurance companies.

items.statement: No patients from Bangladesh now; last year 10% of Agartala volume.
items.quote: Last year around this time, almost 10% of our patient volume was from Bangladesh. At this point, we are not having any patients from Bangladesh. There has been a severe restriction on the number of medical tourism patients coming in.

items.statement: Ranchi project delayed awaiting government approvals; developer pursuing.
items.quote: So the Ranchi project is still something which is under - - we are still awaiting approvals from the government and the developer is following up. But as -- as we are still pursuing that project, it is not like we've given it up.

items.statement: No equity dilution planned; will take debt judiciously, net debt free.
items.quote: We're trying to take debt, right? No equity dilution.

items.statement: Radiation oncology components under installation, to be commissioned in Q4.
items.quote: As guided earlier, the radiation oncology components are under installation and will be commissioned in Q4.

items.statement: Focus on complex treatments like transplants, robotic knee surgeries, higher tertiary care impacting ARPOB.
items.quote: Across all our hospitals, we are focusing on more complex treatments, including transplants, including robotic knee surgeries and other higher tertiary care treatment. So that has definitely impacted the ARPOB.

items.statement: Inpatient volume 23,500 in 9M FY25 vs 23,100 last year, increase of ~400 patients.
items.quote: In terms of our inpatient volume, FY '25, we've had 23,500 patients compared to 23,100 patients in the last 9 months. There has been an increase of around 400-odd patients on a total basis.

items.statement: Evaluating acquisition opportunities in Guwahati, Bhubaneswar, Patna; will disclose later.
items.quote: We have been evaluating opportunities in Guwahati. There are a couple of opportunities at play even right now in a couple of cities like Bhubaneswar or even Patna, but we are evaluating them. We can disclose them later on once we are at a position of finalization.

items.statement: Anticipates gold demand to grow by 12%-15% and silver demand by 15%-18% by end of FY2025.
items.quote: Looking ahead, we anticipate gold demand to grow by 12% -15% and silver demand by 15% -18% by the end of FY2025.

items.statement: Targeting at least 20%-25% growth.
items.quote: Yes, we are definitely aiming to achieve the same growth. However, being conservative, we are targeting at least 20%-25% growth.

items.statement: Planning to raise up to ₹600 crores through QIP.
items.quote: To support our strategic expansion plans, we are planning to raise up to ₹600 crores through the QIP route.

items.statement: QIP proceeds to open company-owned stores.
items.quote: The proceeds from the QIP will be utilized to open company-owned stores.

items.statement: Majority of QIP funds for inventory, smaller portion for CAPEX including store development.
items.quote: Right, we are raising fund ₹600 crores. The majority of the funds will be allocated to inventory, with a smaller portion used for CAPEX, including store development.

items.statement: Aiming to double stores within next 2-3 years, opening 10 more stores.
items.quote: Right. We are undertaking a Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP) to significantly boost our store expansion, aiming to double them within the next 2-3 years. Additionally, we are planning to open a few franchises as part of our growth strategy, pursuing both avenues to achieve our goals.

items.statement: Plan to open 2-3 franchises within next 2 years.
items.quote: We plan to open 2 -3 franchises within the next 2 years, with further expansion to follow. Initially, our focus is on establishing these first few franchises.

items.statement: Aiming to improve current margins, targeting an increase of 20%-25% with focus on wedding, collection, diamond, studded, and Polki jewelry.
items.quote: We are definitely aiming to improve our current margins, targeting an increase of 20%-25% with continued focus on wedding jewelry, collection jewelry, diamond jewelry, studded jewelry, and Polki jewelry.

items.statement: 50%-55% of revenue from wedding jewelry.
items.quote: So, almost like the 50%-55% is coming from the wedding jewelry.

items.statement: White gold and rose gold jewelry contribution is 10% to 15%.
items.quote: So, the White Gold and Rose Gold jewelry contribution is nothing very much, but yeah, 10% to 15% is the total contribution.

items.statement: Inventory price is 8%-10% lower than market, naturally hedged if market falls.
items.quote: So, we are doing the weighted average method. So, our inventory price and market price is different. So, as of now our inventory price is lower than the market around like 8% -10% lower than the market. If market goes down so we are already hedged.

items.statement: Expect organized sector's market share to increase to 50% by FY29.
items.quote: Mandatory hallmarking and rising compliance costs are further steering consumers towards organized jewelry retailers, and we expect the organized sector’s market share to increase to 50% by FY29.

items.statement: New showroom in Neemuch, Madhya Pradesh, spans 7,700 sq. ft. with Ground+3 layout.
items.quote: As per the guidance for FY25 strategic expansion, we launched a new showroom in Neemuch, Madhya Pradesh, during Q3 FY25. This showroom spans a super built-up area of 7,700 sq. ft. with a modern Ground+3 layout, located just 150 kilometers from our registered and administrative office in Ratlam.

items.statement: Second showroom in Ratlam to have carpet area of 12,000 sq. ft., expected launch by end of FY25.
items.quote: Additionally, the construction of our second showroom in Ratlam is progressing well. This showroom will have a carpet area of 12,000 sq. ft., with 8,000 sq. ft. dedicated to retail and the remainder for back-office operations. We expect to launch this showroom by the end of FY25.

items.statement: CAPEX for new stores approx ₹1-2.5 crores; inventory held ₹55-60 crores.
items.quote: This is approx. ₹ 1-2.5 crores capex and inventory which is held at the store is ₹55 cores- ₹60 crores.

items.statement: Stores expected to reach breakeven in around 6 to 9 months.
items.quote: Around 6 to 9 months.

items.statement: Capex for current year will be lower than FY2024 and continue to unwind in FY2026.
items.quote: We believe that our capex for the current year will be lower than FY2024, and this will continue to unwind in FY2026.

items.statement: Capex moderation expected even in FY2026, with capex as percentage of revenues trending downwards.
items.quote: I would say at headline, you should see moderation of capex even in FY2026, and with the revenue growths that we are seeing, the capex as a percentage of revenues will continue to trend downwards and soon be at the levels of global peers.

items.statement: Transferring about 16,100 telecom towers to Indus Towers.
items.quote: we are planning to transfer about 16,100 telecom towers, approximately 12,700 from Bharti Airtel and about 3400 from Bharti Hexacom to Indus Towers.

items.statement: Launching comprehensive cloud solution in next few months.
items.quote: We will be launching a comprehensive cloud solution in the next few months.

items.statement: Postpaid opportunity to reach upwards of 50 million over next few years from 80 million base.
items.quote: There is no reason why we should not get upwards of 50 million over the next few years on postpaid, because there is an 80 million base that is ready to actually get onto postpaid.

items.statement: FWA EBITDA margins similar to home services.
items.quote: Yeah, It will be in that same ballpark.

items.statement: Hexacom addressable market for broadband about 3 to 4 million.
items.quote: In terms of addressable market, I would say this would be about 3 to 4 million.

items.statement: Hexacom has about 2 million home passes currently.
items.quote: About 2 million home passes we have, currently at Bharti Hexacom

items.statement: Hexacom capex directionally same, could marginally increase due to FWA rollout.
items.quote: So, directionally same could be marginal increase, it all depends on FWA rollout.

items.statement: Hexacom dividend payout to be considered positively.
items.quote: Dividend payout is something which will be certainly looked at with a positive angle.

items.statement: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 6.4% in Q3 FY25 from 5.6% in Q3 FY24.
items.quote: 5.6% improving to 6.4% in Q3 FY25, which is a jump of 30% year on year.

items.statement: India multi-channel adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 11.2% in Q3 FY25 from 10.7% in Q3 FY24.
items.quote: We continue to improve our adjusted EBITDA from 10.7% in Q3 FY24, we have improved this by 50 bps to 11.2%, which is a n increase of 20% year on year for Q3

items.statement: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin for nine months FY25 was 5.1%, up from 4% in nine months FY24.
items.quote: And the 4% consol. EBITDA in nine months FY24 has increased to 5.1% for the nine months FY25, which is a n increase of 54% year on

items.statement: Gross margin for Q3 FY25 was 37%, up from 34.5% in Q3 FY24.
items.quote: From 34.5% in Q3 FY24, we have improved this to 37% in Q3 FY25.

items.statement: Gross margin for nine months FY25 was 37.3%, up from 35.4% in nine months FY24.
items.quote: Similarly, for the nine months, the gros s margins has improved to 37.3% compared to 35.4% in nine months FY24

items.statement: International business adjusted EBITDA improved to -15% in Q3 FY25 from -16% in Q3 FY24.
items.quote: From 16% negative EBITDA in Q3’FY24, end of December, we have improved this to minus 15%.

items.statement: Globalbees adjusted EBITDA improved to 1.4% in Q3 FY25 from 0.6% in Q3 FY24.
items.quote: From 0.6% in Q3 FY24, we have improved this to 1.4% in Q3 FY25.

items.statement: Education business adjusted EBITDA for nine months FY25 was around 23%.
items.quote: EBITDA for the nine months is around 23% EBITDA, for Q3 is around 22%.

items.statement: Annual unique transacting customers grew 17% for period ending Dec 2024 vs Dec 2023.
items.quote: Annual unique transacting customers in India and Middle East, 17% increase for the period ending Dec ’24 vis-a-vis period ending Dec’23, annual unique transacting customers.

items.statement: GMV grew 17% for nine months FY25 over nine months FY24.
items.quote: Likewise, our GMV grew for nine months over last nine months by 17% and the net revenue from operation s increased by 19% to INR 5,729 Cr

items.statement: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA grew 54% to INR 293 Cr for nine months FY25.
items.quote: And consolidated adjusted EBITDA grew by 54% for nine months ending Dec’24 vs nine months ending Dec’23 to INR 293 Cr and India multi- channel as well grew by 26% for the same nine month period resulting into overall cash profit after tax of 47% increa se for the similar nine months to INR 139.7

items.statement: GMV increased 13% in Q3 FY25 over Q3 FY24.
items.quote: GMV increase in Q3 is 13%.

items.statement: Expects 15-20% revenue growth over next 3 years.
items.quote: So, next 3 years, we are looking at the growth rate of around 15% to 20%. Although, we will target to achieve more, but 15% to 20% definitely we will be able to achieve and EBITDA margins, we expect the EBITDA margins to be at the same, similar lines across the product.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to remain similar across products.
items.quote: and EBITDA margins, we expect the EBITDA margins to be at the same, similar lines across the product.

items.statement: Chennai plant phase 1 capacity ~55-60 crores, phase 2 total ~100-110 crores.
items.quote: Basically, we are going to put a CAPEX at Chennai plant in phase 1 and phase 2 and in phase 1, approximately, in value term, the capacity will be approximately 55 to 60 crores and phase 2, which will be happening in next year, we will be touching the overall capacity in Chennai in value term approximately 100 and 110 crores.

items.statement: Chennai plant commissioning expected by Q1 FY26.
items.quote: We expect that this plant would be commissioned by Q1 of FY’25-26.

items.statement: Investing 11 crore in Wada plant for various machines.
items.quote: So, we will be investing this CAPEX of 11 crore in different machines, in the Disc Spring, Coil Spring, and Fastener as well.

items.statement: Strong order book and pipeline support growth momentum.
items.quote: We have a strong order book and pipeline, which gives us confidence of continuing our growth momentum.

items.statement: Offers 15-18% price saving vs German producers in export market.
items.quote: Yes, so basically when we compete with German producers in the export market, we are able to offer about 15% to 18% price saving as compared to the German prices and in terms of India of course, we are the market leaders in our products, particularly for spring.

items.statement: In India fastener category, offers 3-4% saving vs local suppliers.
items.quote: In fastener category in India, we are able to offer 3 to 4% saving because customers are looking more technical solutions, more customized suppliers rather than only price saving as compared to their local suppliers.

items.statement: Renewable and industrial to drive growth 30-40%, mobility 20-25%.
items.quote: I think, broadly, renewable and industrial will be the major drivers of the growth that will be about 30 to 40% and mobility will be about 20-25%.

items.statement: Export and domestic mix to remain 35-40% exports, 60% domestic.
items.quote: So, broadly the export and domestic mix will remain same which is about 35 to 40% exports and about 60% will be domestic even going forward.

items.statement: No major impact expected in next 1 year from US renewable uncertainty.
items.quote: But based on the discussion with customers of course in last couple of weeks we do not see any major impact in next 1 year because most of the projects are allotted.

items.statement: Wada plant max revenue potential 325-350 crore.
items.quote: Going forward with some incremental CAPEX we will be able to achieve around 325-350 crore from Wada itself.

items.statement: Fastener segment growth expected higher than other product groups.
items.quote: So, I think company level we are looking at about 15 to 20% growth CAGR for next 3-4 years and of course fastener being a much smaller base and we just started adding more and more customers more and more segment. So, growth in fasteners will be higher than the other product groups category.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to stabilize at 15-18%.
items.quote: Post COVID in fact year on year we are able to improve our EBITDA if you see our last 4 year performance and going forward we are thinking we should be stabilizing this EBITDA level 15-18-17 something and so there will be quarter-on-quarter there will be some plus and minus but because of the various reason or product mix or some one time cost and all.

items.statement: 68 crores of IPO funds unutilized, to be used for Chennai and Wada capex.
items.quote: Major portion of the 78 crores 68 crores is actually unutilized IPO funds which has been kept in fixed deposit which will get utilized for the Chennai and Wada CAPEX over the period of next 6 months to 1 year.

items.statement: Expects at least 15%-20% growth next year with new products.
items.quote: So, if everything goes well, then we are looking at growth of at least 15%-20% for the next year with these new products coming in pipeline.

items.statement: Seamless tube project capex approximately INR170 odd crores, starting Q4, majority in FY26.
items.quote: We would be starting our investments in quarter 4 for the seamless tube plant. And the majority of it would be done in FY26. The total value of the capex on the seamless tube project is approximately INR170 odd crores.

items.statement: Seamless tube project completion targeted mid-FY27, orders for imported equipment by end of FY25.
items.quote: We anticipate the completion of this project within 18 months, targeting mid-FY27.

items.statement: IPO proceeds of approximately INR70 crores allocated to capex, in line with plan.
items.quote: But we had basically, from the proceeds of the IPO, we had set out approximately INR70 crores on our capex. This is mainly on the enhancement of our forging capabilities and our new line in the foundry and as well as new machines for us to equip us to ramp up on our production of our exports.

items.statement: February order book approximately 4,000 axles.
items.quote: However, we've seen good growth in the month of January and our order book of February is approximately of 4,000 axles.

items.statement: Expects better EBITDA margins in Q4 and ahead, especially with exports.
items.quote: But within Q4 and going ahead, we will see better EBITDA margins coming in. And especially with the exports going up, we would deliver better EBITDA margins and profitability as well.

items.statement: Export business could run at 20% to 22% EBITDA margin.
items.quote: The margins, fortunately, are much better. I mean, if we are to draw our balance sheets only based on export business, we would be running with an EBITDA of 20% to 22%.

items.statement: Backward integration into seamless tubes to reduce cost by 3% to 4%.
items.quote: Now, the effect of it will be about 3% to 4% on the cost of the product. If we go in for our own backward integration and use the tubes which we manufacture ourselves, they will cost about 3% to 4% lesser than our existing route.

items.statement: Q4 demand from trailer business is good and strong.
items.quote: And more importantly, we see Q4, the demand from the trailer business is quite good, quite strong.

items.statement: Component business improving, OEM volumes getting better.
items.quote: The component business is getting better. Volumes at OEMs are getting better.

items.statement: Launched 18-ton axle and two mechanical suspensions; car carrier axle and suspension launching this quarter.
items.quote: What we are going to get into in this quarter will be the launch of the car carrier axle and suspension. This product aims at trailers, which are specifically designed to carry cars and bikes from the OEM to the various dealers and everything.

items.statement: Extrusion plant to increase capacity to 7,500 units per month from 5,000.
items.quote: This advanced technology will increase our capacity to 7,500 units per month, up from our current 5,000 trailer capacity for axles and suspension assemblies.

items.statement: Employee cost increase was one-off, will revert to previous percentages from coming quarters.
items.quote: But this is, you could say, it is a one-off case in this quarter. It's going to be back at our previous percentages from the coming quarters.

items.statement: Exports to reach 15% of revenue in next 2 to 3 years.
items.quote: 15% of our revenue coming in from exports in the next 2 to 3 years. That's what I was explaining.

items.statement: Exports expected at 5% of revenue this year, around INR25 crores-INR28 crores.
items.quote: So, we are looking at 5%, around INR25 crores-INR28 crores revenue coming in this year from the export front.

items.statement: Seamless tube investment of INR167 crores funded through debt and internal accruals.
items.quote: This will involve an investment of INR167 crores and this will be funded through a mixture of debt and our internal accruals.

items.statement: Anticipates double-digit growth in Q4 on a year-to-year basis.
items.quote: We feel that the situation has now improved quite a lot and we are anticipating double-digit growth in Q4 on a year-to-year basis.

items.statement: Secured INR1,089 crores order from Vedanta Limited, a four-year contract till 2028.
items.quote: your company was able to secure a landmark INR1,089 crores order from Vedanta Limited, which we feel is one of the largest orders in Indian multimodal and supply chain solutions. This four-year contract which will go on till 2028, covers the entire gamut of transportation and logistics of their several products such as aluminium ingots, billets, wire rods, pig iron and EXIM shipments from their pl

items.statement: Received INR170 crores order from Hindustan Zinc Limited for logistics of finished goods for four years.
items.quote: We also received about a month ago an order of INR170 crores from the world's largest and India's only integrated zinc, lead and silver Western Carriers ( producer, which is Hindustan Zinc Limited. This is also for logistics of their finished goods, which includes zinc and lead ingots for a period of four

items.statement: Materials handling contract from Vedanta for import and domestic EXIM operations at Jharsuguda, value INR139 crores.
items.quote: Another contract that we have which is corollary to the INR1,089 from Vedanta is the materials handling contract from them for both their import and domestic, EXIM operations, again at the Jharsuguda plant. And the order value of that is INR139 crores.

items.statement: Domestic volumes grew 24%, offsetting 15% decline in EXIM container volumes for 9M FY25.
items.quote: The domestic volumes at the same time have shown a growth of 24% which has successfully offset this about 15% decline in EXIM container volumes for the first 9 months.

items.statement: Margin improvement too early to say, but should happen in the long term.
items.quote: So margin improvement it's too early to say, sir, because all of these new projects and work is in progress, but margin improvement should happen in the long term for sure, sir.

items.statement: Faucetware capacity utilization at 91%, Sanitaryware at 90% in Q3 FY25; expansion to 4 lakh units/month yielding positive results

items.statement: Aiming for 1% improvement in consolidated EBITDA margin over the next year and a half
items.quote: So keeping all of this in mind, we are still aiming for 1% improvement in EBITDA margin going forward at a consol level in the year and a half ahead.

items.statement: Three new facilities under construction adding ~1,100 machines in MP, ~750 machines in Karnataka, and a 200-machine leased unit in Ranchi (400 machines equivalent on 2 shifts), all expected to commence in FY26
items.quote: The first one is a new facility in This will increase the capacity by about 1,100 machines and is under construction. The second one is an additional unit in Karnataka, which will add about 750 machines, which is also under construction. The third incremental unit is expected in Ranchi leased premises. All these units are expected to commence operations at different points in FY '26

items.statement: Order book remains strong with good fall/winter placements and strong early indications for spring/summer
items.quote: The company's order book remain strong, securing robust near-term prospects. Fall/winter order placements have been good, the production for which happens in Q1 and Q2. Early indications for spring/summer is also strong.

items.statement: Matrix at ~14% EBITDA margin, Atraco at ~7%; targeting 10% for Atraco next year, Matrix at par or above Gokaldas standalone
items.quote: So I think Matrix is at about 14-odd percent and Atraco is proportionately, I think 7% or thereabouts.

items.statement: Raw material prices are a pass-through; cotton prices have dropped and should remain range-bound with no rapid spike expected
items.quote: Our business, if I look at only the garmenting business, which is bulk of our business, is really a conversion business. So we really do not -- our raw material prices are really a pass-through. So if there is a price increase or price decrease, we tend to pass it back through to our customers.

items.statement: U.S. retail apparel sales grew 3% in CY24; U.S. and EU imports picked up in H2 CY24 as retailer inventories normalized, supporting demand bounce-back
items.quote: U.S. retail apparel sales remained consistent, showing a 3% growth in calendar 2024. U.S. and EU apparel imports have picked up momentum since the second half of CY '24 on the strength of lower inventory with retailers.

items.statement: Outerwear ~30% of Gokaldas 9M revenue (~35% annualized); Matrix and Atraco low single digits; polyester/synthetic growing but fabric still sourced from Far East
items.quote: So outerwear on a 9-month basis for Gokaldas was about 30%.

items.statement: New capacity ramp-up depresses margins for 1-1.5 years; MP Phase 1 ramp-up added INR3-4 cr cost in Q3 without proportionate revenue; Kenya shilling appreciation pressuring Atraco margins
items.quote: So our incremental cost was about INR3 crores to INR4 crores on account of all of this, and it has not manifested in proportionate revenue. So that's -- that was the point I was referring to.

items.statement: Incremental revenue potential: MP Phase 2 ~INR175 cr, Karnataka ~INR125-130 cr, Ranchi ~INR55-60 cr, Atraco 500-machine expansion ~INR125-130 cr, knit fabric unit ~INR150-200 cr annually
items.quote: The incremental capacity in MP should net in about INR175 crores when it is fully ramped up. I'm talking of the incremental new capacity. One in Karnataka would yield about INR125 crores, INR130 crores. And the one in Ranchi would yield about INR55 crores, INR60 crores. So overall, I would say it's about INR300-odd

items.statement: Invested INR175 cr in BTPL via OCDs to date; further ~INR588 cr (adjusted for working capital) needed for 100% acquisition; merger process to initiate June 2025 via NCLT, taking 9-12 months
items.quote: So, till this quarter that is quarter ending December, we have invested INR110 crores in - BTPL and subsequently we have invested another INR65 crores. So, it amounts to about INR175 crores of investment till date.

items.statement: Top-end of 10-15% revenue CAGR over 2-3 years is a reasonable assumption; $1 billion revenue vision attainable in a few years
items.quote: I think it's a very decent assumption. I would say that top end of that range will be a more reasonable decent assumption.

items.statement: BTPL standalone peak revenue ~INR1,500+ cr at 12-14% EBITDA; consolidation not before FY27; will reduce fabric import dependence for synthetics but not eliminate it
items.quote: So the impact of BTPL, if I look at it on a st and-alone basis, its peak revenue could be about INR1,500-plus crores. But then again, a lot of it could be bought internally. So once it is merged, some of those revenues will get knocked off in consolidation

items.statement: No near-term M&A; focus on integrating acquisitions from last 9 months; multi-shift operations difficult in South due to women workforce transport constraints; INR depreciation hedged through Q1-Q2
items.quote: We want to consolidate what we have. Remember, we have only taken up some of these acquisitions 9 months ago, and there is tons of work required to be done to bring them to where we would like them -- like to see them.

items.statement: No significant preponement of orders due to tariff fears; buying is seasonal and India-sourced orders not seeing pull-forward; Africa may benefit if tariffs rise on other regions
items.quote: So I'm not seeing much of that happen out of here. And also the worry on tariff is more on the Far East. So there may have been some degree of expediting of deliveries from China, maybe even Vietnam and all of that. But then as far as the India denominated sourcing is concerned, we are not seeing so much of that.

items.statement: MP unit PLI not applicable due to product HS codes; DBT from MP government expected to start flowing next financial year, providing margin lever beyond 250 bps
items.quote: So, in terms of accounting we are taking and we are at -- we were told by the MP government that it would start flowing from the forthcoming financial year and we should -- we should start seeing that. So, we are on track for it.

items.statement: Q4 margins directionally better than Q3 due to seasonal strength and MP ramp-up completion; not speculating on exact numbers
items.quote: Yes. So see, Q4 is seasonally good. Directionally, it should happen. And again, let's not speculate on those margin number. But yes, directionally, we will be going in that -- on that trajectory.

items.statement: Mining capacity expansion approval for Ari Dongri mines from 2.35 to 6 million ton expected by Q1 FY26
items.quote: The approval for mining capacity expansion of Ari Dongri's mines from 2.35 million to 6 million ton is expected to be in place by Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: Pellet plant capacity increase from 2.7 to 4.7 million ton expected to be commissioned by Q2 FY26
items.quote: The increase in pellet plant capacity from 2.7 million to 4.7 million ton is expected to be commissioned by Q2 FY '26.

items.statement: Greenfield integrated steel plant of 2 million ton dropped; evaluating smaller capacity of 0.8-1 million ton with lower capex
items.quote: The plan to set up a greenfield integrated steel plant with a capacity of 2 million ton has been dropped. Company is evaluating different alternative projects with lower capacity and lower capex for which announcement will be made once the project is finalized.

items.statement: OPVC pipe manufacturing project dropped; capex was INR125 crores, only INR14 crores spent, supplier agreed to return money
items.quote: The plan to venture into OPVC pipe manufacturing has been dropped due to changed market scenario.

items.statement: Remaining capex for new pellet plant INR432 crores to be spent over next 4 months; trial production expected early Q2 FY26
items.quote: So between Q4, which is already going halfway. So next 4 months, the entire remaining INR432 crores will be spent. And we are confident we can start the trial production of the new pellet plant in FY '26, Q2.

items.statement: FY26 capex estimated at INR1,000 crores covering mining, beneficiation, pellet plant, solar for mining and pellet
items.quote: So roughly capex of about, say, INR1,000 crores to INR100 crores will be spent in FY '26.

items.statement: Healthy order book for pellets till March end; inventory down to below 20,000 tons from 1 lakh tons
items.quote: And the end of December, the market picked up, and we have a healthy order books. So it was a one-off situation where prices were a little corrected, plus we had a higher inventory than we maintained.

items.statement: Pellet margin ~INR4,000/ton (cost INR6,000, selling price INR10,000); steel value-add margin INR5-7/kg from sponge to finished
items.quote: So our pellet cost is about INR6,000 per ton and the average selling price is about INR10,000. So we make a margin of about INR4,000 on pellets on ex plant basis. And we sell finished, which is wire rod and HB wire. So if you see from sponge because sponge is captive. So from sponge to a finished sale and with all the infra and the power cost, we make about INR5 to INR7 there.

items.statement: Export pellet realization currently INR1,000/ton less than domestic market on net basis
items.quote: Okay. So if you export right now, the realization will be about INR1,000 less compared to domestic market.

items.statement: India steel demand projected to grow 8-9% in 2025 driven by housing and infrastructure construction
items.quote: India's steel demand is projected to grow by 8% to 9% in 2025, driven by increased construction in housing and infrastructure sector.

items.statement: High-grade pellet production to increase from 35% to ~80% with new capacity; commercial grade 20% for domestic market
items.quote: So going forward, our high grade will be close to about 80% and 20% will be the commercial grade, which is in the domestic market.

items.statement: 8 million tons of additional pellet capacity (excl. GPL) commissioning in next 6-8 months in Chhattisgarh and Maharashtra
items.quote: So apart from Godawari, about 8 million tons of pellet plant is being commissioned in the next 6 to 8 months, which is a good capacity.

items.statement: FY26 pellet production guidance 3-3.25 million tons (2.5M current + 0.5-0.7M new plant); FY27 full 4.5 million tons
items.quote: So FY '26, we'll do about 3 million to 3.25 million tons of pellet. But FY '27, we should do about 4.5 million tons of pellets

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA estimated at INR500-800 crores additional from new pellet plant at current market scenario
items.quote: To be honest, 4.5 million capacity of pellet and plus addition everything bare minimum is about INR50 crores to INR800 crores of EBITDA FY '27.

items.statement: Revised steel plant capex ballpark INR3,500 crores for 0.8M ton or INR4,000 crores for 1M ton capacity
items.quote: For example, if we do a 0.8 million capacity or 1 million capacity, the figure be somewhere about INR300 crores to INR400 crores. If you even consider INR400 crores to INR 450 crores per 1 lakh ton of steel. So 0.8 million, INR3,500 crores for 1 million, probably INR4,000 crores.

items.statement: Acquired 49% stake in Jammu Pigments on fully diluted basis as of 31 Dec 2024; share of profit INR50 lakhs for 40 days
items.quote: GPL has completed acquisition of 49% stake in share capital of Jammu Pigments Limited on a fully diluted basis as on 31st December '24.

items.statement: FY26 Vanillin capacity utilization guidance of 75% remains unchanged
items.quote: FY26, yes. That's right. That guidance remains.

items.statement: Blends business expected to grow 15-20% for next few years
items.quote: I think we've been growing the business in excess of 15% to 20%. And that will continue to grow at that level, at least for the next few years.

items.statement: FY26 capex plan of Rs 30-35 crores, largely maintenance
items.quote: The CAPEX plan is about, roughly about Rs. 30 crores to Rs. 35 crores.

items.statement: Vanillin cost to reduce ~10% at 100% utilization from current $8.50-9.00/kg
items.quote: 100% utilization, the cost from where we are today should come down by about 10% or so.

items.statement: Vanillin pricing improved ~10% vs last quarter; US prices up ~20%
items.quote: I mean it's improving, it's about 10% better than it was in the last quarter.

items.statement: Catechol+Vanillin breakeven at ~70% Vanillin utilization; Vanillin alone breakeven at ~40%
items.quote: I think at about 70% of Vanillin utilization, Catechol and Vanillin lines should breakeven.

items.statement: Vanillin contracts for FY26 minimal; Europe certainty expected by June
items.quote: From Q1 of FY26, there's hardly any contracted, very small quantities contracted.

items.statement: Blends growth driven by new customer acquisition across all regions at 15-20%
items.quote: Yes, so it's basically customer acquisition in all the regions. We are growing all regions at about 15%-20% with new customer acquisitions.

items.statement: Europe diphenol wind-down losses to reduce from ~Rs 55-60 cr annualized to Rs 20-25 cr
items.quote: we should be able to annually bring it down to an annual cost of between Rs. 20 crores to Rs. 25 crores.

items.statement: China operations loss ~Rs 3-4 cr per quarter, expected to reduce next year
items.quote: China is not bleeding like Vanillin, though there is a loss. We are getting around Rs. 3 to 4 crores per quarter.

items.statement: Rights issue Rs 224 cr: Rs 100 cr repaid NCD, Rs 68 cr reserved for debt repayment, Rs 56 cr general corporate
items.quote: Rs. 100 crores we have used for repaying the LCD which we borrowed in the last quarter. We are reserving around Rs. 68 crores for debt repayment and for the general corporate purpose Rs. 56 crores.

items.statement: Gross debt ~Rs 600 cr after NCD repayment; expect ~Rs 550 cr by end FY26
items.quote: So by the end of next year, we expect to be around Rs. 550 crores from Rs. 600 crores right now?

items.statement: Vitafor integration complete; targeting 20-25% growth in FY26, then 20%+ annually
items.quote: the integration is complete. And now the focus will be in F Y26 to grow that business by at least 20% to 25

items.statement: US Vanillin prices ~$12-13/kg; anti-dumping duty 187% preliminary in US
items.quote: The US is, of course, not our entire business is not in the US. It's only a part of our business is to the US. And the Vanillin prices are in around $12-$13 range.

items.statement: Continuing operations EBITDA ~Rs 70 cr (Q3 reported Rs 53 cr + Rs 17 cr discontinued loss)
items.quote: It will be about Rs. 70 odd crores.

items.statement: Vanillin plant at 50-55% utilization currently, targeting 70% by year-end, 75% FY26
items.quote: As I said, we are working at around 50%-55% and we will be moving to 75% by this year.

items.statement: Target residential debt at INR1,000 per square foot of area under development
items.quote: From the residential debt perspective, our target is always to maintain at INR1,000 a square foot and under of area under development.

items.statement: Target IRR in high 20s to early 30s for redevelopment and outright projects pre-cost of capital
items.quote: But should it be a redevelopment project or an outright purchase, your IRR will be in high 20s and early 30s.

items.statement: Deploy balance HDFC fund capital of over INR700 crores before June 2025
items.quote: The balance capital, which is a little over INR700 crores is expected to be deployed before June of this year.

items.statement: Launch pipeline of 12.63 million sq ft with 73% planned projects in non-Bengaluru markets
items.quote: Our launch pipeline for the comp any is robust with approximatel y 12.63 million square feet of the new planned projects with non-Bengaluru projects now accounting for 47% of the share of ongoing and 73% of planned projects

items.statement: Evaluating equity raise via QIP, AIF, platform-level funding to optimize financing structure
items.quote: We are also focused on maintaining optimal financing structure, including raising equity through QIP, AIF, platform level funding, etcetera.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin around 10%; 9M FY25 total income up 16% YoY with comprehensive loss of INR99 crores
items.quote: EBITDA margins for the quarter were around 10%, while we had a net loss of INR94 crores. For the 9 months ended for this financial year, our total income increased by 16% Y-o-Y, while the total comprehensive loss was approximately INR99 crores.

items.statement: Average realization up 16% YoY to INR8,847/sq ft in Q3 FY25; Puravankara up 29%, Provident up 7%
items.quote: Average realization for the quarter has also increased by almost 16% Y-o-Y to INR8,847 per square feet because of the mix of inventory, while Puravankara and Provident saw 29% and 7% Y-o-Y increases, respectively.

items.statement: Expect OC for Capella, Atmosphere, Oakshire, Adora De Goa in next 2 quarters with 3.95M sq ft salable area and INR3,200 crores GDV
items.quote: Further, we are expecting occupancy certificates for the projects like Capella, Atmosphere, Oakshire and Adora De Goa in next 2 quarters with total salable area of 3.95 million square feet with total GDV of INR3,200

items.statement: Land investments of INR1,236 crores in 9M FY25; business development of ~7M sq ft with GDV over INR12,000 crores
items.quote: On business development front, we have done land investments of approximately INR1,236 crores during the 9 months of the financial year. We have done business development close to 7 million square feet with GDV over INR12,000 crores during this time.

items.statement: Sales growth CAGR 57% and collections CAGR 58% over last 3 years; area delivered CAGR 47%
items.quote: Our sales growth has grown at CAGR of 57%, while collections have increased at a CAGR of 58%. The area delivered has expanded at a CAGR of 47%.

items.statement: Expect manufacturing EBITDA margin of Rs. 7 per liter average for next year with 20-25% volatility range
items.quote: Yes, that's what we expect for next year to be around Rs. 7 a litre. The other thing is, there's this new policy that has been announced and contrary to some of the statements I've made on earlier calls about volatility of margins, we now expect margins to be extremely range bound. My sense is an average of 7 for the year and maybe 20%-25% plus minus from there.

items.statement: Expect capacity utilization to run at full tilt next year after prioritizing maintenance in Q3-Q4
items.quote: Absolutely. So, that's exactly the point. In Q3 and Q4, we have prioritized a lot of our maintenance activities, which would have happened in the coming quarters or in the coming year. So, the plan now is to be running at as close to full tilt as possible.

items.statement: Prestige and above revenue vision of Rs. 500 crore in 3-4 year window
items.quote: So, from the current strategy that we have in place, we have a vision to take this to about Rs. 500 crores type of revenue. But the concern on that is I am not able to give you a timeline or an accurate timeline. But that's certainly in the 4-5 year kind of window, maybe 3-4 year window from now.

items.statement: Expect IMFL Prestige and above to break even in at least one quarter next year
items.quote: I think it looks like breakeven is around the corner for the division. I hope in the next year, we are certainly expecting to break even in at least one quarter, maybe more.

items.statement: No large capex planned currently beyond UP distillery commissioning in Q2 FY26
items.quote: No, large CAPEX planned currently.

items.statement: Secured sufficient warehousing capacity for maize procurement ahead of upcoming season
items.quote: For maize procurement, we have secured sufficient warehousing capacity ahead of the upcoming season to ensure a steady supply of maize at fixed prices.

items.statement: Manufacturing EBITDA margin was 1% in Q3 with Rs. 0.85 per liter, down from 4% in Q3 FY24
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the manufacturing business stood at 1% in Q3 consistent with Q2, but lower than 4% in Q3 FY24. Margin per liter came in at Rs. 0.85 per liter, reflecting the cost pressures faced in the segment.

items.statement: Consumer regular category EBITDA margin 15% in Q3, down from 17% in Q2 due to packaging cost inflation
items.quote: EBITDA margin in this category stood at 15%, slightly lower than 17% in Q2 due to inflationary pressures on packaging costs.

items.statement: Prestige and above EBITDA margin improved to -10% in Q3 from -24% in Q2
items.quote: The EBITDA margin improved to minus 10%, which is a notable recovery from minus 24% in Q2.

items.statement: Rajasthan announced 4.35% price increase for country liquor, large portion expected to flow to EBITDA
items.quote: We have announced that it's increased by 4.35%. It's not 4.35 across all brands or across all categories. So, we have to see how the year shapes out, but suffice it to say a large part of it will flow down to EBITDA.

items.statement: UP regular category sold 13,000 cases last month, volumes can become very interesting next year
items.quote: We have done last month, I believe, 13,000 odd cases in UP regular category. So, let's see how it shapes up, but it can become very interesting next year.

items.statement: Luxury portfolio (Terai, DŌAAB) growth projected higher than mainstream; dedicated division created
items.period: H1 and H2 of coming year
items.quote: We have created a dedicated division for our luxury brands, which includes a dedicated team and a strategy to accelerate growth of these luxury products, namely Terai and DŌAAB,. This initiative will focus on premium positioning, brand development, and ensuring additional new product launches in H1 and H2 of the coming year.

items.statement: FCI rice supply expected to start in second part of February; raw material volatility to reduce by end March
items.quote: But even still, but as we speak today FCI delivery of raw material has not yet started. We expect that to begin in the second part of February at some point. So, some part of cost decrease has taken place. Another part will take place once supply starts. So, my sense is by end March or mid-March, we would firmly be in the new pricing environment and thereafter it will become range bound from there

items.statement: FCI arrangement seen as stop-gap for 1-2 years until maize cultivation scales; long-term focus on maize procurement and corn oil efficiency
items.quote: I see FCI is a stop gap arrangement. I see FCI for one year, maybe two years to help the industry transition to maize. Maize cultivation too needs to grow. We have seen very good growth in the winter crop, but that's pretty much a South and West India focused crop. We are hoping for good growth in the summer crop as well. It's looking pretty good so far. So, another year or two of this kind of gro

items.statement: UP distillery commissioning expected in Q2 FY26; will enable margin parity with Rajasthan for regular category
items.quote: Our UP multi-feed distillery project is progressing well with commissioning expected in Q2 FY26. Once commissioned, this facility will help grow profitability in the state, as well as provide supply security as brand volumes grow.

items.statement: Malt spirit production facility recently commissioned; enhances cost efficiency and supply security for luxury brands
items.quote: In addition, our malt spirit production facility has recently been commissioned. This will allow us to enhance our cost efficiency and also drive innovations, aside from ensuring a steady stream of quality malt spirit for our brands and thereby giving us supply security.

items.statement: Arun 3 hydro project commissioning expected in last quarter of FY27
items.quote: And during the last quarter of the financial year '27, we will commission the Arun 3.

items.statement: Buxar thermal project first unit COD targeted for May, second unit 4 months later
items.quote: Buxar just May month, next -- within 2, 3 months, we are going to commission first unit. 660megawatt first unit, we are going to commission during the month of May. COD during the month of May. Mohit Kumar: And the second one, sir? R.K. Chaudhary: Second one, it will take another 4 months

items.statement: Total capacity addition of roughly 3 GW targeted for FY26 including 1.5 GW solar and 1.3 GW thermal
items.quote: So we would be able to add roughly around 1.5 gigawatt of solar in FY '26. And thermal side, we would be adding this 1.3 gigawatt of thermal. These are -- so if you put together, it is around, say, roughly 3 gigawatt of capacity, which company is going to add in FY '26.

items.statement: Another 1.5 GW renewable capacity addition expected in FY27
items.quote: So '27, we will be adding another 1.5 gigawatt of project from our renewable portfolio.

items.statement: Target to add roughly 3 GW capacity every year from FY26 onwards to reach 25 GW by 2030
items.quote: every year, we are going to -- by FY '26, we are going to add, say, roughly around 3 gigawatt of capacity every year

items.statement: Hathidah Durgawati pumped storage project cost estimated at INR 5,663 crores
items.quote: The project cost is estimated at INR5,663 crores with a levelized tariff of INR9.39 per kilowatt hour.

items.statement: MOU signed with Bihar for 1,000 MW Hathidah Durgawati pumped storage plant
items.quote: One of the major developments in this quarter is the signing of an MOU with the Government of Bihar on 31st December 2024 for development of 1,000 -megawatt Hathidah Durgawati Pumped Storage Plant in Bihar.

items.statement: MOU signed with Rajasthan for 5 GW pumped storage and 2 GW floating solar projects
items.quote: Another important development is the MOU signed with the Energy Department, Government of Rajasthan on 20th November 2024 for the development of renewable energy in the state. Under this partnership, SJVN will develop 5 gigawatt pumped storage projects and 2 gigawatt floating solar projects in Rajasthan.

items.statement: Awarded capacity of 2.4 GW achieved in FY25 as REIA
items.quote: And overall, SJVN has achieved an awarded capacity of 2.4 gigawatt during this financial year.

items.statement: PSA signing delays causing gap between awarded and under-construction REIA capacity
items.quote: Yes, we have already received the tenders and the gap is because of the PSA, power sale agreement and signing of PPA. So once we tender for as REIA, then we approach various DISCOMs. And once the power sale agreement is signed with the interested DISCOM, then we sign the PPA, power purchase agreement with the developer.

items.statement: Arun 3 facing geological challenges at dam site causing commissioning delay to Q4 FY27
items.quote: But unfortunately, at dam site, we are facing certain geological challenges. And because of that geological challenges, the commissioning is expected to be -- to get delayed. And during the last quarter of the financial year '27, we will commission the Arun 3.

items.statement: Bikaner solar project delayed due to module supply issues from Tata EPC contractor
items.quote: Bikaner, as the EPC was awarded to Tatas and their factory, they could not commence the production of modules in time. So it's an issue industry -wide issue.

items.statement: SJVN Green Energy listing targeted for Q3 or Q4 FY26
items.quote: Maybe in the third quarter, we will be able to -- this issue -- we'll try to listing in the third or fourth quarter.

items.statement: Foreign currency exposure of INR 3,400 crores in USD and INR 1,500 crores in JPY
items.quote: As of now, we have borrowing in USD and JPY. We have outstanding of roughly INR3,400 crores in the USD and around INR1,500 crores in JPY. That's our exposure as on date.

items.statement: Q3 incentive income of INR 68.49 crores vs INR 51.18 crores in Q3 FY24
items.quote: For Q3 incentive is INR68.49 crores. And during last year, similar quarter, it was INR51.18 crores.

items.statement: Total generation of 10,084 MU in 9M FY25, up 26.3% from 7,987 MU in 9M FY24
items.quote: Overall, from all our plants, we have achieved 10,084 million units as of now compared to 7,987 million unit, which is an excess generation of 2,097 million unit, which is 26.3% ahead more compared to the last year's generation.

items.statement: Order book exceeds INR 14,200 crores with 58% EPC and 42% O&M mix, 40-60 domestic-international split
items.quote: With a robust order book exceeding INR 14,200 crores, we maintain a healthy mix of 58% EPC and 42% O&M projects, and a 40-60 split between domestic and international projects.

items.statement: Secured 75% of INR 3,500 crores preferred bidder projects into confirmed orders
items.quote: During our Q2 call, we had informed you all that Wabag is a preferred bidder status for projects worth approximately INR 3,500 crores. We are pleased to report that we have already secured 75% of these opportunities into confirmed order.

items.statement: Medium-term EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 13% to 15% window
items.quote: You would see the 13% to 15% window remaining clear. You see the 9 months number that we have last year to current year, we are at 13.5 %. That remains steady.

items.statement: Medium-term revenue growth guidance of 15% to 20% over 3-5 years reaffirmed
items.quote: This was given for a medium term, which is 3 to 4 or 3 to 5 years, in our personal meeting, which we did in May last year. On that front, we are very, very confident.

items.statement: Bank limits tied up for INR 4,000 crores, expected to increase to INR 5,000 crores within FY25
items.quote: We already have bank limits tied up for INR 4,000 crores, which we expect to increase to INR 5,000 crores within this fiscal year.

items.statement: Pipeline robust for decades in emerging markets driven by urbanization and infrastructure needs
items.quote: See we are in the emerging markets. As we said, where infrastructure is required, urbanization is happening. So, pipeline is robust, will remain robust for the decades to come.

items.statement: O&M margins slightly higher than EPC, more predictable and sustainable
items.quote: As far as margin is concerned, rightfully said, it is more predictable, more in grip. So, margin would be slightly higher than the normal EPC.

items.statement: No execution capacity constraints; manpower per million revenue decreasing with larger ticket sizes
items.quote: So, we have always grown with the orders, and we believe we have enough strategy in place in recruiting and hiring people, training people, developing them under the NATs, NAPs, all schemes which government has given us.

items.statement: Price escalation clauses in contracts cover 70-75% of costs based on RBI indices for projects over 18 months
items.quote: Always, always. B ecause our contracts are always long -term contracts, especially in India, anything more than 18 months, we always have a price escalation built in where the government of India RBI indices will be the basis

items.statement: Al Haer Saudi order: INR 3,251 crores consortium, Wabag share ~INR 1,725 crores (55%), 30-month execution
items.quote: Our order what will be passing through our books will be about INR 1,725 crores or something. So, INR 1,725 crores will be passing through our books and the rest of it. So, about 55 % odd should pass through our books.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 revenue expected to be bumper quarter, maintaining full-year guidance

items.statement: FY25 operating income growth guidance of 12% to 13% with EBITDA around 11%

items.statement: Project Lakshya to contribute 65% to 70% of revenue by FY26

items.statement: Target FY2026 revenue mix: 75% flights, 25% non-air (currently 86% flights)
items.quote: So, our target is that in FY2026, we should be able to say 75% of our business came from flight and 25% business came from all other sectors, which right now is at 86%.

items.statement: Middle East GBR grew 227% YoY to INR 170 crores in Q3 FY2025; growth seen as sustainable but lumpy
items.quote: Our Dubai operations have also shown remarkable progress, showing a year-on-year growth of 227% and the gross booking revenue stood at INR 170 crores in Q3 FY2025.

items.statement: Hotel nights booked grew 172% YoY to 2.5 lakh in Q3 FY2025, contributing 11.1% of GBR
items.quote: This quarter, total nights booked stood at 2.5 lakhs, reflecting a significant 172% year-on-year growth and contributing 11.1% to the gross booking revenue.

items.statement: Reduced discount rate from 3.8% to 3% QoQ while GBR still grew 7% YoY
items.quote: We took the call of reducing our discounts for this particular quarter and yet there was an increase in GBR, which we see as a positive sign.

items.statement: EV bus manufacturing initiative underway; will take a few more quarters to come to shape
items.quote: So, the EV buses, what we started off in the manufacturing mix, that is going to take more few quarters' time to completely come in shape.

items.statement: Promoter Nishant Pitti sold 1.4% stake; public commitment not to sell further shares this year
items.quote: Nishant has already taken a public stand saying that he has sold 1.4%, not 14%, which was incorrectly mentioned in the media. And yes, for this year, there will be no selling from the promoter side.

items.statement: Acquired Planet Education Australia to enter study tourism sector
items.quote: Furthering our expansion into specialized travel services, we have entered the study tourism sector with the acquisition of Planet Education Australia.

items.statement: Plant-2 extension is now fully operational.
items.quote: In line with our strategic road map, Plant 2 extension is also now fully operational.

items.statement: Plant-6 brownfield project acquired last quarter will be built out to reach INR1,000 crores revenue capacity.
items.quote: along with Plant-6 which is the brownfield project that we acquired last quarter, we will build that out and then by finishing that we will reach INR1,000 crores

items.statement: Upcoming capex primarily for Plant-6 oral solid expansion; layout and machinery selection in progress.
items.quote: I think that one upcoming capex will be primarily for Plant-6 bringing up which is the oral solid expansion and we are in the layout and machinery identification selection process.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 12.3% for 9M FY25 and 12.6% for Q3 FY25 despite injectable facility depreciation increase.
items.quote: EBITDA surged by 22% Y-o-Y to INR68.6 crores, 12.3% margin for 9-month FY '25 and by 21% Y-o-Y to INR24.6 crores, 12.6% margin for Q3 FY '25.

items.statement: Injectable facility expected to first cross breakeven then contribute to operating leverage over 3-4 years.
items.quote: as the injection facility starts to generate revenue and it will first crossover breakeven and afterwards start contributing to the margin so operating leverage will begin to come in the numbers

items.statement: Long-term ROCE target around 27%-28% despite ongoing capex for oral solids expansion.
items.quote: in long range we want to stay 27% - 28% likes of ROCE and more

items.statement: Trade Generics & Institutional vertical grew 44% Y-o-Y in 9M FY25 and 74% Y-o-Y in Q3 FY25.
items.quote: In 9-month FY '25, revenue surged to INR126.6 crores marking a 44% Y-o-Y increase. For Q3 FY '25, revenue increased to INR49.6 crores registering 74% growth Y-o-Y.

items.statement: CDMO vertical grew 15% Y-o-Y in 9M FY25 and 8% Y-o-Y in Q3 FY25; volume growth historically flat to low single digits.
items.quote: This vertical recorded a 15% Y-o-Y increase in 9 months FY '25 to INR407.9 crores. For Q3 FY '25, this vertical generated INR135.7 crores in revenue witnessing an 8% Y-o-Y growth.

items.statement: Schedule M enforcement driving smaller competitor closures; compliant players like Windlas benefiting from customer shift.
items.quote: The surprise audits are happening across the spectrum and we have also received audits and have passed in flying colors and continue to. I believe even smaller many companies in different CMO belts like Baddi and even near Uttarakhand have had these audits and have been closed down.

items.statement: API price reductions passed through in cost-plus model; conversion impacted but neutral over long term.
items.quote: API prices have fallen down and there has been obviously some effect on conversion. But having said that, there has also been increase in past and so API prices tend to have some impact because ours is a cost plus model. In the long run it gets pacified for plus as well as minus in API prices.

items.statement: Existing order book in place for injectable production; products ready for commercialization from stability batches.
items.quote: There is already some order book in place for our existing production happening and products getting ready for commercialization and out of stability batches.

items.statement: Sufficient oral solids/liquids capacity for ~INR800 crores revenue with Plant-2 expansion now online.
items.quote: So we have sufficient capacity for our oral solids and oral liquids business to reach across about INR800 crores. This is aside of injectables.

items.statement: Targeting KFC brand contribution margin of 19-20% at about 100,000 ADS over a few quarters
items.quote: we are targeting KFC to get to 19 to 20% margin at about 100,000 ADS , and we are tracking on that . It will take us a few quarters to be able to get there , but on an overall basis , we are confident that the kind of measures we have taken and once they start to kick in, we will be able to see the full results at about 100,000 KFC ADS with 19 to 20% brand contribution margins.

items.statement: Plan to add 20-25 KFC stores in Thailand (8-9% growth) and target 3-4% SSSG for ~11-12% revenue growth in FY26
items.quote: As far as the store growth is concerned, Thailand represents the largest opportunity. We plan to add about 20 to 25 stores, which is 8 to 9% of the stores that we have. And then on top , we are targeting a SSSG of about 3 to 4% which should give us about 11 to 12% revenue growth.

items.statement: Will moderate Pizza Hut expansion further; future expansion dependent on brand performance
items.quote: Going forward, as we have spoken in the past, we will be moderating Pizza Hut expansion, and you will see even further lower numbers versus what we have done so far. So, we continue to remain bullish on KFC . On the other hand, we have added new brands. We are monitoring Pizza Hut performance very closely. And therefore, depending on the brand performance, we will take a final call on the numbers.

items.statement: Focus on small format stores for capital efficiency and stronger payback potential
items.quote: A key driver of this has been our focus on small format stores over the past few years which are highly capital efficient and offer stronger payback potential.

items.statement: Consolidated brand contribution margin improved 70 bps QoQ to 14.3% due to sales leverage and cost optimization
items.quote: The brand contribution for Q3 FY25 stood at 14.3%, higher by 70 basis points versus the previous quarter. Improvement in brand contribution was mainly on account of sales leverage and fresh measures on cost optimization in the Indian and Nigerian operations.

items.statement: KFC brand contribution margin improved 60 bps QoQ to 17.2% due to sales leverage and cost optimization
items.quote: The brand contribution margin at 17.2% for the current quarter saw an improvement of 60 basis points because of better sales leverage and cost optimization measures.

items.statement: Pizza Hut brand contribution margin at 2.1% in Q3; margin improvement expected from next quarter via marketing cost optimization and fresh cost measures
items.quote: we will see margin improvement coming from next quarter because we are optimizing the marketing cost in Pizza Hut versus what we have done in the last 6 to 9 months. At the same time, we have taken some fresh cost optimization measures also in Pizza Hut as well as KFC, which will start to yield the results from January onwards.

items.statement: Costa Coffee brand contribution margin improved to 16.9% in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Brand contribution in Q3 saw an improvement and stood at 16.9%.

items.statement: International brand contribution margin improved 60 bps QoQ to 16.6% in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Brand contribution margin at 16.6% saw an improvement of 60 basis points versus Q2 FY25.

items.statement: Gross margin dropped 60 bps QoQ to 68.7% due to food inflation in oil, chicken, cheese, coffee beans
items.quote: The gross margin for the consolidated business was 68.7%, a drop of 60 basis points versus the previous quarter. The impact on gross margins was primarily due to food inflation that we have seen in core brands, driven by rising oil, chicken, cheese and coffee bean pricing.

items.statement: Seeing green shoots of recovery in metros and large cities during festive season; value menu items driving volumes
items.quote: While the overall consumer sentiment remained a little subdued , during the festive season our QSR in general and DIL witnessed some green shoots of recovery in the metro and large cities. For the budget conscious consumers, Value Menu Items such as KFC Roll Variants and Snackers were major attractions during the festive season.

items.statement: Three new QSR brands planned for launch from Q1 FY26 (April onwards)
items.quote: Yes, we are on track from Quarter 1 of the next financial year.

items.statement: Opened first food court under JV with PVR INOX at Kota (51% economic interest); not fully consolidated per auditor opinion
items.quote: We opened our first food court under the strategic tie-up with PVR INOX at Kota. DIL has an economic interest of 51% in the new Company. Please note that this entity shall be consolidated in accordance with Accounting Standards 28.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 sales volume trimmed to 4.6-4.8 million sq ft and sales value to INR 2,400-2,700 crores
items.quote: Based on our sustainable sales expectation for Q4 and contribution from the 2 launches that are expected this quarter, we are constrained to trim our full year number to about 4.6 - 4.8 million square feet. Sales values go down to some extent.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 handover target of 1,500 units vs 1,300 units last year
items.quote: We are setting ourselves with a targeted Q4 handovers of about 1,500 units as compared to 1,300 units that we did last year.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 EBITDA margin (excl. other income) guided at 22-25%, PBT margin 9-11%, PAT margin 8-10%
items.quote: We believe EBITDA without other income can reasonably stabilize between 22% - 25% at any point of time on an annual basis. Quarter-to-quarter fluctuations will always be there because of base effect.

items.statement: Medium-term target to nearly triple annual revenue by FY28 from ~INR 1,000 crores base
items.quote: On a medium-term basis, as we have said, we are looking at more than nearly tripling our revenues on an annual revenue recognition by FY '28, which is a 3 years plan that we have articulated publicly.

items.statement: Next year (FY26) top-line growth of at least 20% driven by 3-5 million sq ft handover momentum
items.quote: handover momentum of our -- completion and handover momentum of about 3 million to 5 million square f eet should give us at least a 20% growth on an annual basis in the top line. Can be higher, but for now, I will stay with 20

items.statement: New project investments of ~INR 40 crores in Q3 FY25
items.quote: We made new project investments about INR ~40 crores. Therefore, we ended up consuming cash from closing cash and equivalents.

items.statement: Acquired 3 new projects with 1.1 million sq ft development potential and GDV of INR 850-1,000 crores
items.quote: Shriram Properties has acquired development rights for 3 new projects in Yelahanka, which is North Bangalore; Electronic City in South Bangalore; and Koyambedu in Chennai with a combined development potential of 1.1 million square feet and a gross development value of about INR 850 crores to INR 1,000 crores.

items.statement: Target to double launch pipeline from 17 million sq ft to 30-35 million sq ft over next 12-24 months
items.quote: As we have set out to achieve our medium-term aspiration, we need to nearly double our pipeline from 17 million square fee t launch pipeline to over 30 million square feet in the next 12 to 18 months, max 24 months

items.statement: Q3 FY25 gross margin ~31%, EBITDA margin ~24% (incl. other operating revenue), PBT margin ~8%
items.quote: Overall, margins remained healthy, that clearly shows that the projects that are getting recognized have a healthy margin profile. Gross margins are about 31%. EBITDA margins were about 24%, 8% PBT margins.

items.statement: Portfolio price hikes ~5% in FY25 so far after ~20% growth in FY23-24; mid-market avg realization ~INR 6,700/sq ft
items.quote: Overall, price remains stable. Our portfolio price hike is in the range of about 5% during the year so far, appreciable modesty in price hikes because we have had very robust price hikes over the last 2 years, 20% growth in our portfolio price averages between FY '23 and '24.

items.statement: Customer activity revived strongly post festive season (late Oct 2024); no demand slowdown, only administrative delays
items.quote: Customer activities have revived post the beginning of festive season, midway through October-November 2024. We have seen a remarkable bounce back in customer activity; therefore, we remain positive about the underlying market conditions.

items.statement: Kolkata launch contingent on KMDA final approval (50% probability by mid-March); royalty dispute provisioning continues (INR 4 cr in Q3)
items.quote: The plan approval is received. But the KMDA last final approval is awaited still, and therefore, I'm not really raising hope on it, but it has a equal probability of coming through towards the second half of March.

items.statement: No definitive promoter buyback plans; index fund inclusion not yet eligible due to size
items.quote: On the question of promoter buying, there are no definitive plans right now. We'll come back to you if there any plans which is approved by the promoters as well as the shareholders.

items.statement: Land monetization in Chennai yielded INR 93 cr cash (mostly Q4); INR 5-6 cr capital gain recognized in Q3
items.quote: We have completed land monetization in Chennai and the cash flows of about INR 93 crores are received now, and that has augmented additional capital for growth for us.

items.statement: Gross debt reduced to INR 470 cr, net debt INR 400 cr; target net debt reduction but balanced with growth capital needs
items.value: Gross INR 470 cr, Net INR 400 cr
items.quote: Today, we've got a gross debt of INR 470 crores, net debt of INR 400 crores. So even on a net basis, we are down from INR 440 crores to INR 400 crores on a gross basis, reflecting these repayments, we have come down substantially from INR 631 crores to INR 470 crores.

items.statement: Current financial year topline will be more or less flat; bottom-line growth much higher, in line with current run rate
items.quote: So, to conclude, I wish to reiterate, while the current financial year topline will be more or less flat as indicated in the past, the bottom-line growth would be much higher, more or less in line with our current run rate we have achieved till now.

items.statement: 9-month bronze bushing sales around Rs. 60 crores, on track to cross Rs. 80 crores annual target
items.quote: Thus, the 9 months year-to-date sales for bronze bushing is around Rs. 60 crores plus, very much in line with our expectation of crossing Rs. 80 crores annual sales target of bushing this financial year.

items.statement: Major sourcing contract for cages with large global customer concluded; considerable additional business expected from second-half of FY26
