items.quote: I am thinking like one week, maybe max two weeks is when we will be able to close the FCCP round and similar timelines for the preferential bonds too, because there are a lot of questions back and forth from the NSE, BSE we are answering those by.

items.statement: Margin improvement driven by operational efficiencies and AI tool productivity gains
items.quote: The margin improvement is primarily driven by efficiencies that we are able to squeeze out of the system itself, we found some inefficiencies, and we squeezed that out. The second thing that I told you earlier also is, we are able to get more performance improvement using some of these AI tools that we are actively using in our day-to-day outrange.

items.statement: No impact from Trump tariffs on IT services; customers continuing as before
items.quote: But from a services side, there is no impact so far there is no focus on services except, the outlook is that there will be deregulation, specifically on the AI side and the cloud side and so on and so forth. Which will improve IT services business in the US.

items.statement: No customer course changes yet; potential government sector opportunities from deregulation
items.quote: Have any of our customers made any changes? As of now there are no changes; they are continuing as they are. It's too early to say, there is speculation with respect to what might happen, but from a perspective of our customers changing course or doing something different, we don't see that happening.

items.statement: LIC contract milestone payments ongoing; next large chunk expected within three months
items.quote: We did get some payment in a way or once we met the milestone, the next milestone is probably within the next three months we should get a large chunk of the money coming in.

items.statement: Growth focus on AI-enabled services and account mining existing customers
items.quote: We are targeting growth in the AI and AI enabled services. That is one area of target that we are going after, and we are seeing a lot of traction in that. And also, the second thing that we have been doing is we are doing a lot of account mining, so I have given a target to our senior management team that we need to start getting more revenue from existing customers.

items.statement: No plans to enter new geographies; addressing challenges in existing ones
items.quote: We don't want to enter new geographies, we already have enough geographies that we have, there are some challenges with some of the geographies that we are facing, and we have been addressing that, but at this point, no.

items.statement: FY26 sales target around 2,600 crores, aiming to cross that level
items.quote: We expect FY '26 to be much better and the sale ex pectation is around 2,600 crores. That's what the budget that we are preparing. It's a little short of 2,600 crores, but our target is to cross 2,600 crores in '26

items.statement: FY27 revenue target of 3,000 crores and FY28 around 3,200 crores
items.quote: in the year 27, we had said we would be touchi ng around 3,000 crores. That still stands. We should cross that. And in 28, we should be around 3,200 crores

items.statement: Export revenue expected to recover from 360 crores this year to over 500 crores next year
items.quote: And in the export front, like I mentioned, from 360 crores, this year, we should go to about almost 500 crores.

items.statement: Board target remains 13% EBITDA margin, expected to be achieved by FY27
items.quote: Our target is still the same. It's the 13% margin that the Board has given us a very clear direction and we are working in that direction.

items.statement: US tariff uncertainty on exports; awaiting PM Modi-Trump meeting outcome, may need alternatives if tariffs imposed
items.quote: If there are tariffs imposed, that is one thing we are all waiting for. By tomorrow morning, I think there would be total clarity on this. But we are hoping that this would stay. Otherwise, we will have to look at alternatives as to what else w e need to do so that we do get our goods into the U.S. market

items.statement: Customer launch postponements remain a recurring risk; experienced delays in past two years
items.quote: And the second thing is that the customers don't p ostpone the launch of the new vehicles. We experienced it last year. We did experience it year before last year also. But we are hoping that there would be no postponement

items.statement: Cost reduction initiatives: power savings from melting changes and renewable energy, manpower reduction via Rico Production System, further reductions expected as volumes grow
items.quote: we have been able to save power primarily because of the changes that we made in our melting areas and also the solar energy, solar as well as our hybrid, the wind. And in the manpower cost also we have been able to be, we have started using our Rico Production System, which is very eff ective where we have been able to reduce manpower a lot, and as the production goes up and the new lines start a

items.statement: Full year FY25 volume guidance of 100-115 million meters; expect to be at lower end
items.quote: For the full year FY '25, we will be at a lower end of our volume guidance of 100 million to 115 million meters.

items.statement: Full year FY25 EBITDA margin guidance of 15% to 16%
items.quote: For the full year, FY '25, we will be at guided EBITDA margin range of 15% to 16%.

items.statement: Aspire to double consolidated revenues by 2028 driven by core, utility bedding and brands
items.quote: We want to reiterate that at a consolidated level we aspire to double our revenues by 2028, driven by our core business, utility bedding and brands, including our recently added licensed brands.

items.statement: FY25 capex estimate of Rs. 463 crores including Rs. 65 crores normal capex and Rs. 50 crores for US plant
items.quote: Rs. 463 crores to be precise.

items.statement: Greenfield pillow facility in North Carolina with $15 million investment, 18 million pillow capacity, revenue from September 2025
items.quote: The new facility will have a production capacity of 18 million pillows with a total investment of $15 million financed through 75:25 debt to equity structure to start with. With a gradual roll out and revenue build up targeted from September 2025

items.statement: Recent acquisitions Fluvitex USA, Modern Home Textiles USA and new licensed brands contributed approximately Rs. 100 crores in Q3
items.quote: Our recent acquisitions Fluvitex USA, Modern Home Textiles USA, and new licensed brands have started contributing to revenues, achieving approximately Rs. 100 crores in Q3.

items.statement: Near-term US investments to impact margins by 150-200 bps till March 2026
items.quote: The near term investments in US will impact margins by 150 to 200 basis points till March '26.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA margin 14.2% impacted by product mix, promotions, team building and higher shipping costs
items.quote: Our EBITDA for Q3 FY '25 was Rs. 165 crores, a growth of 14% year-on-year, with an EBITDA margin of 14.2%.

items.statement: US retail sales showed strong growth in Q3 FY25 fueled by holiday spending; Red Sea issues behind us, freight rates stabilized
items.quote: During Q3 FY '25, US retail sales have shown strong growth fueled by holiday spending, reinforcing market confidence.

items.statement: Utility bedding category size $4-4.5 billion at US retail; acquired two facilities and building third on East Coast to serve bulky products locally
items.quote: Similarly, utility bedding is a similar category with $4 billion to $4.5 billion in revenue at retailers side. Utility bedding consists of pillows, mattress protectors, mattress pads, down alt comforters.

items.statement: Cotton prices at Rs. 55,000-56,000 per candy ex-mill; current warehouse stock lasts till Q4, potential benefit from Q1 FY26
items.quote: So, cotton prices are at around Rs. 55,000 to Rs. 56,000 candy, ex- mill. And of course, at Indo Count we use multiple types of cotton, we import cotton, we use domestic cotton.

items.statement: 50-60% of forex exposure hedged at ~Rs. 85.50; rupee depreciation benefit as hedges roll off but must consider competitor currency moves
items.quote: In terms of FOREX, we are 50% to 60% hedged at any point of time, so of course our hedges, which have already been taken place, are at around Rs. 85.50 levels.

items.statement: Gross debt ~Rs. 1,300 crores (Rs. 1,000 crores working capital, Rs. 300 crores long-term); expect gross debt to remain at similar level next year
items.quote: Gross debt is Rs. 1,300 crores roughly. This is on a consolidated basis.

items.statement: Domestic business ~2.5% of revenue with two brands Layers and Boutique Living; high focus area for growth
items.quote: At this point of time, we are roughly at around 2.5% of our overall revenue comes from our domestic business.

items.statement: Wamsutta brand launch targeted for Q1 FY26; acquired global trademarks and IPs plus licenses for Fieldcrest and Waverly
items.quote: With Wamsutta's market positioning strategy now in place, we are gearing up for a successful launch in Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: US utility bedding facilities in Arizona and Ohio at ~50% capacity utilization; expect sequential quarterly improvement
items.quote: These new facilities that we have already in Arizona and Ohio already, today, as we speak, are touching 50% capacity utilization. So, we expect quarter-on-quarter better results from new businesses to come.

items.statement: Management targets continuing long-term average growth rate dependent on consumer demand recovery
items.quote: we really target just continuing our long-term average growth rate

items.statement: FY25 capex spend about Rs 150 crore; FY26 budget not finalized yet
items.quote: FY25, we have got a spend of about Rs.150 odd crore for the whole year. And FY26 budget has not been finalized yet

items.statement: Chennai greenfield facility to be commissioned in current quarter adding less than 10% capacity
items.quote: Chennai is going to start with one printing line. So, on the overall capacity, we will be adding less than 10% to the overall capacity

items.statement: EBITDA margins steady at 15% in Q3; flexible packaging growth may slightly reduce blended margins but similar return on capital
items.quote: Our EBITDA grew by 29%, reaching Rs. 71 crore, with margins steady at 15%

items.statement: Raw material price changes are temporary as business passes through cost increases or decreases to customers
items.quote: Largely, we get a pass-through or we have to give a pass-through to customers. So, it's a temporary effect, if anything, and our business is quite agnostic on the raw material price

items.statement: Domestic consumer demand weak in low single digits; banking on recovery from tax cuts and moderating inflation
items.quote: Consumer demand has been a little bit weak in India the last few years. And the growth rate has been in a very low single digit

items.statement: Flexible packaging growing faster than paperboard; Creative Offset targeting high double-digit growth
items.quote: Flexible packaging tends to be a lower margin business, but you get a similar return on capital because it's a higher asset turn. As that grows, to that extent, margin can come down a little bit

items.statement: Creative Offset revenue expected ~Rs 50 crore this year with high double-digit growth next year
items.quote: this year we should do about Rs. 50-odd crore. So, in the coming year we hope to definitely increase that in very high double-digit rate

items.statement: Liquor decartonization not reversed; 90% volume lost but offset by new customer development
items.quote: the decartonization has not really reversed. But brands are launching new offer packs and launch like rebranding and all with the carton. But 90% of the volume has sort of gone from that segment

items.statement: Exclusive manufacturing agreement with Ventit for ventilated pizza boxes; no capex required, only working capital
items.quote: we are excited to announce our exclusive manufacturing agreement with Ventit, a pioneer and patent holder in ventilated pizza box technology

items.statement: Capacity utilization at 80%+ with headroom for growth; Chennai plant adds capacity with room for further expansion
items.quote: we are at about 80% plus kind of level. Now we are just adding Chennai, and we just added some capacity in Goa. In the coming year, we have a few capex plans, but broadly, 80% plus sort of level

items.statement: Innofilms merged into flexible packaging; teething issues largely resolved and used as marketing tool for sustainable solutions
items.quote: Innofilms we merged into flexible packaging segment, I mean, into the company only. So, now that doesn't get reported separately, but the performance has improved, and we are quite optimistic on the output

items.statement: Creative Offset at EBITDA breakeven with small cash loss; expected to improve with higher utilization
items.quote: Creative is an EBITDA breakeven and a small cash loss. That we see improving in coming months as the utilization

items.statement: Export markets include Europe, Middle East, Africa, USA, North America, Southeast Asia, neighboring countries
items.quote: we are exporting to Europe and Middle East. We are exporting to Africa, now the USA and North America has also been added. We are exporting even to Southeast Asia. We are exporting to our neighboring countries

items.statement: Pharma packaging limited to OTC brands; prescription segment requires specialization not yet pursued
items.quote: we are a very small player in this field. We mostly service OTC, like the branded sort of pharma where you can recall the name of the product

items.statement: Expect to cross INR800 crore revenue in FY25, potentially INR815-820 crore if momentum continues
items.quote: So I think we are definitely on a track to cross INR800 crores. Now let's see how this quarter 4 ends, but we are definitely looking -- if the same momentum comes, I think we'll be doing INR815 crores, INR820 crores or something like that.

items.statement: Targeting return to 18%+ consolidated EBITDA margin guidance from Q4 FY25
items.quote: We are going back on our original guidance of 18%. We still do not -- on the operations side, I think nothing is wrong. The margins are there, but this notional which we do take for the UK.

items.statement: QIP proceeds of INR125 crore allocated: INR62.5 crore for capex (moulds, machinery, new facilities), INR5 crore utilized so far, major spend in FY25-26
items.quote: We have a capex allocation of INR62.5 crore, which includes investment in moulds, machinery, new facilities. Till now we have utilized around INR5 crore because the major capex plan is underway, which will be utilized in FY '25, '26.

items.statement: New factory to be constructed on land opposite existing facility for built-in appliances expansion, may also serve Quartz expansion
items.quote: A new factory will be constructed on the land opposite to existing facility to support above expansion plans in the built-in appliances. If required, we may use this land for further Quartz expansion business.

items.statement: Major customer Karran USA awarded huge order from biggest US home retail chain, expecting large order flow this quarter requiring fresh mould investment
items.quote: Finally, we are pleased to inform you that our major customer, Karran USA has been awarded a huge order by one of the biggest US home retail chains, and we are expecting a large flow of orders from them by this quarter.

items.statement: IKEA approved second SKU for global requirements, expecting 10-15% sales rise from IKEA business
items.quote: We are expecting a 10% to 15% rise in sales with the IKEA business.

items.statement: Secured starting order with Kohler India for stainless steel sinks, deal value ~$1 million annually
items.quote: The deal value could be about $1 million a year to start with, but it's a good starting point with such a global company.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin impacted by US subsidiary loss, GBP translation loss (INR2.8 cr), freight cost increase (INR2.1 cr), MMA cost increase (INR0.7 cr)
items.quote: EBITDA, margin for quarter 3 FY '25 was impacted mainly due to reasons like the export freight cost increased from 6.5% in March '24 to 9.3% in December '24 due to Red Sea issues. This has resulted in impact of margin by INR2.1 crore on Q-on-Q basis.

items.statement: All Q3 margin headwinds reversing in Q4: freight rates back to pre-March levels, GBP strengthened to INR108+, MMA price falling to $2.02/kg
items.quote: Every factor coming from the export freight to exchange to raw material price, everything in the cycle is getting reversed. So whatever the factor was affected in quarter 3, all the factors getting reversed in the current quarter itself.

items.statement: Quartz sink plant utilization at 65% in Dec 2024, expected to improve to 80% in coming quarters of FY25-26 driven by Karran and IKEA orders
items.quote: As of December 31, 2024, our plant capacity utilization stood at 65%. We are also happy to inform a second breakthrough by the new SKU has been approved by IKEA for their global requirement and will overall improve our capacity utilization to 80% in the coming quarters of FY '25, - '26.

items.statement: Domestic business flat in Q3 due to soft market and Delhi pollution shutdown, expecting value-driven growth in coming quarters from new high-margin products
items.quote: Our domestic business remained relatively flat quarter 3 FY '25 due to softer market conditions. However, we expect a more value-driven growth in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Launched high-margin Quartz sink models for India and international markets, stainless steel sinks, and kitchen faucets; invested INR35 crore in new moulds and machinery
items.quote: We have successfully designed high-margin models for Quartz sink for the international and the Indian market, along with the stainless steel sinks and a large variety of high-margin kitchen faucets to cater the domestic industry. To support the development, we invested over INR35 crores in new moulds, machineries, utilities and new products.

items.statement: Introducing workstation sinks (INR25-40k retail), high-end Quartz models, built-in appliances (refrigerators INR2-3 lakh), AI-driven smart appliances, ovens with air fryers, premium faucets (INR20-25k)
items.quote: Now we have a completely different category of the model, the high-end market, which is now compromising. Already, we expect in quarter 4 about 10% of our sales will be of high-end margin products.

items.statement: US subsidiary (United Granite) at break-even in Q3, targeting profitability from Q1 FY26 via cost optimization, supply chain changes, showroom closure
items.quote: As we already stated this quarter will have break-even at the operating level, it will not be a loss. And going forward from quarter 1 onwards, we see that it turn into the profitable.

items.statement: Employee cost benchmark at 10% of sales; current increase due to skilled workforce hiring for future capacity expansion and new product launches
items.quote: So basically -- I'll tell you, we have cost benchmark like 10% of the sales. If anything in that range, it's all acceptable because number one, we are growing and also we need to have more talented manpower.

items.statement: 75 KLPD biodiesel plant in Bathinda expected to commission in next 3-4 months, estimated capex around 120 crores
items.quote: The Company is also currently setting up a 75 KLPD biodiesel plant in Bathinda, which will support complete vertical integration in ethanol production. This we expect to be commissioned in the next three to four months. The estimated CAPEX for the project of biodiesel is around 120 crores.

items.statement: 250 KLPD ethanol plant and 20 TPD bio-CNG plant at Goyal Distillery Fatehabad, total capex around 370 crores, timeline 18 months for ethanol plant and at least 2 years for bio-CNG
items.quote: I think including the bio-CNG, the paddy straw-based power plant and the distillery, I think we are looking at around 370 crores of CAPEX in total.

items.statement: Distillery EBITDA margin expected to return to at least 10-11% with raw material price correction and edible oil exit
items.quote: I think the Company will go back around to at least 10-11% of EBITDA margin from the distillery segment.

items.statement: Distillery segment revenue expected at 1,750-1,800 crores; biodiesel at full capacity ~250 crores; Kharagpur unit at full capacity ~750-800 crores
items.quote: See, the distillery should give us about 1,750 to 1,800 and the biodiesel once working at 100% capacity utilization should give us anywhere close to 250 crores of revenue. But for the first year, we are not taking 100% capacity utilization because there will be somewhat of a learning curve as we are entering a new industry. And with the Bengal unit working at 100% capacity utilization should give

items.statement: Maize prices corrected from ~27.5/kg last quarter to ~25.5-25.8/kg currently; FCI rice at Rs 22.5/kg expected to further reduce raw material costs
items.quote: Last quarter they were hovering around 27.5 per Kg and this quarter they are somewhere around Rs. 25.5 to Rs. 25.

items.statement: At maize price ~Rs 24/kg, profitability similar to FCI rice at Rs 22.5/kg given current DDGS prices
items.quote: considering the current prices of DDGS of both rice and maize, if they are to remain the same, then once maize is around Rs. 24, I think profitability will be the same in both the sectors.

items.statement: Ethanol volumes rose 26.9% YoY to 48,845 KL in Q3; PML segment sold ~13.2 lakh cases, momentum expected to continue
items.quote: The distillery segment demonstrated robust growth with ethanol volumes rising by 26.9% to 48,845 KL. Revenue from the ethanol segment reached 350 crores with a steady 37.8% increase year-on-year, while the distillery segment EBITDA stood at 42 crores, reflecting a 14.2% decrease year-on-year.

items.statement: Phased exit from edible oil segment by Q1 FY26, freeing 90 crores working capital and reducing debt; real estate divestment proceeds for further debt reduction
items.quote: BCL is undergoing a key transition with a phased exit from the edible oil segment to enhance profitability and operational focus. The exit is expected to be completed by Q1 FY '26, freeing up 90 crores in working capital and significantly reducing the debt on the Company.

items.statement: Ethanol price from maize not expected to increase; biodiesel selling price ~Rs 104/litre; ENA realization stable at Rs 69-70/litre; Rajasthan ENA contract fixed at Rs 77/litre including transport and duty
items.quote: No, I don't think there will be an increase in the price of ethanol from maize.

items.statement: Goyal Distillery 250 KLPD plant will not qualify for interest subvention scheme as commissioning deadline passed
items.quote: The Goyal Distillery will not be under interest subvention. Although it was approved for interest subvention, the deadline for commissioning has passed. So, that will not fall under interest subvention.

items.statement: Company plans to raise 60-70 crores debt for 150 KLPD ethanol and 75 KLPD biodiesel projects; overall debt to decrease due to 90 crore working capital release from edible oil exit
items.quote: For now it is coming out of internal accrual, but I think the Company will look to raise about, get about 60 to 70 crores in debt for these two projects.

items.statement: FCI rice allocation tender filled for 15-17% of annual quantity; results expected in a day or two; FCI rice policy valid till September end (sugar year)
items.quote: We have filled in about 15 to 17% of our quantity to be from FCI rice and on an average throughout the year. So, let's see what the tender results are.

items.statement: 1,150 KLPD total capacity (including 150 KLPD expansion) estimated to generate ~2,800 crores revenue at full utilization
items.quote: 1,150 would be, I think around, depends on the, it's not price in the future, but, approximately, I think it should be around 2,800 crores.

items.statement: SEBI show cause notice regarding undisclosed promoter entity; case adjudicated, settlement application filed, awaiting resolution
items.quote: So, I think the show cause notice from SEBI, I think it was regarding an entity which they said should be considered as promoter, which was not declared as promoter entity and I think the case has been adjudicated and we will come up with the resolution soon.

items.statement: Biodiesel plant limited to 75 KLPD due to raw material constraints; 50% feedstock from in-house corn oil, rest from market (acid oil, used cooking oil, fatty acid)
items.quote: See, raw material being an issue. Of course, we could have added a bigger plant, but raw material is an issue. As I just mentioned, 50% of raw material will be in-house and the rest we have confidence that we will be able to procure from the market. But we did not foresee that we will be able to procure too much raw materials in one place.

items.statement: Expects PAT of Rs 1,800-2,000 crore for FY25 and similar earnings for FY26, but warns of significant drop (>50-60%) in FY27 post Revlimid
items.quote: I mean, we believe that this year we will probably end up with about Rs 1,800 to 2,000 crore PAT. and that's our expectation. We are still hopeful that we will meet that guidance. Even next year, I think our expectation is that we will be able to do that

items.statement: Expects one-third allocation of Revlimid market starting March 2025 quarter
items.quote: I think, as you are aware, we will get almost one-third allocation of the total market as per our settlement and that will start kicking in the next quarter.

items.statement: Semaglutide India launch targeted for March 2026 subject to regulatory approval; focusing only on injectable, not oral
items.quote: India launch, as you are aware, my friend, I think subject to regulatory clearances and other issues, March 26 is the India launch.

items.statement: Risdiplam India launch pending Delhi High Court verdict; shared FTF with Sun Pharma
items.quote: Another launch, which is a very interesting launch, is Risdiplam. In India, we have litigated in Delhi High Court. The judge has reserved the matter and hopefully, if we have a positive verdict, we can launch that as well.

items.statement: Crop Health Sciences targeting Rs 120-150 crore revenue in FY26 to approach breakeven from current ~Rs 60 crore
items.quote: Our target is that we should target about 120 to 150 crores next year so that will help us come closer to break even.

items.statement: Warns of significant earnings drop (>50-60%) in FY27 due to Revlimid patent expiry; volatility inherent to business model
items.quote: You should expect a drop, a significant drop. But, you know, whether it will end at 50%, 60%, I mean, it all depends on, you know, how that year goes.

items.statement: US tariffs on Indian pharma would impact industry; only mitigation is acquiring US front-end manufacturing
items.quote: The only escape is you need to buy a front-end manufacturing in the U.S. That's the only way you can go forward. That's the only solution.

items.statement: Finance cost from short-term borrowing (bill discounting, advance tax) at ~6% vs 8% deposit yields; debt ~Rs 200 crore
items.quote: It's 200 crores of debt that we have. About 100 crores is what you call foreign bill discounting. 100 crores are tax payments that we make for the advance tax.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guided at 10%-12% from core operations
items.quote: We are on target this year to grow around 10% and we expect to continue the growth momentum in the next year as well where we may again grow at 10%-12%.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth expected above 15%
items.quote: 27 onwards, we expect to more than 15% growth.

items.statement: Order book stands at Rs. 16,396 crores as of Dec 31, 2024
items.quote: As of December 31st, 2024, our order book stands at Rs. 16,396 crores with 64% coming from hydropower, 21% from irrigation, 10% from tunneling and the remaining from other sectors.

items.statement: Targeting Rs. 10,000-12,000 crores order inflow in next one year
items.quote: So, see, we are targeting at least Rs. 10,000-Rs. 12,000 crores order inflow and accordingly similar inflow may happen in the next year as well.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected around 13%-14% for next year
items.quote: Yes, somewhere around that range only, 13%-14%.

items.statement: Capex requirement of Rs. 150-200 crores for expected order inflow
items.quote: CAPEX for order inflow what we expect Rs. 150-Rs. 200 crores.

items.statement: Non-core asset realization targeted at Rs. 200 crores per year
items.quote: So, we expect Rs. 200 crores year-on-year for the next couple of years.

items.statement: Strong project awarding expected in calendar year 2025
items.quote: While project awarding activity was muted in the first three quarters, we expect a strong flow of large-scale projects in this calendar year, providing ample opportunities.

items.statement: Hydro and PSP combined constitute 70% of Rs. 30,000 crores bids submitted
items.quote: So, in terms of hydro, irrigation and tunneling, see hydro and PSP combined is almost 70% and rest other segment is balance 30% out of which irrigation is around 7%-8%.

items.statement: US subsidiary litigation of $15-20 million sold with entity, no impact expected
items.quote: So, it may be somewhere around $15-$20 million.

items.statement: Debt reduced by over Rs. 450 crores to Rs. 1,422 crores consolidated
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, our debt stands at around Rs. 1,422 crores as compared to Rs. 1,885 crores at the end of the previous year, March 24. Hence the debt has come down significantly by more than Rs. 450 crores in this year.

items.statement: Land monetization potential of Rs. 200-300 crores over next 3 years
items.quote: So, if we have to look from land monetization, maybe Rs. 200-Rs. 300 crores.

items.statement: Management cannot provide any guidance for AUM growth or credit costs for next year or even next month until things stabilize
items.quote: I cannot even give you a guidance for next month. I am kind of joking, but the fact is any guidance is meaningless at this point.

items.statement: Marginal cost of borrowing is 11.2% while blended cost for nine months is 12.86%
items.quote: So marginally, I would say it's about 11 and a quarter. If you include everything else in it… Vivek Modi: That's about a quarter for the nine months turning out to b e about 12.86. But the incremental cost or the marginal cost as Alok said is 11.2

items.statement: Zero DPD flow forward rates improved to 98.03% in December and 98.15% in January, with February month-to-date showing 35-40 bps further improvement
items.quote: Now that being said, we have seen at least for the last two months, zero DPD flow forward rates have been 98% plus. So I think it was 98.03 in December and 98.15 in January.

items.statement: Management estimates about 20% of customers in the industry are stressed, with 80% paying on time
items.quote: I would say about 20% of the customers are stressed in the industry. And why I say that 20% number is that 80% of my customers pay me on the second that it is due, the money.

items.statement: Write-offs for the quarter were Rs. 45 crores in Namra and Rs. 4 crores in Arman standalone, totaling ~Rs. 50 crores
items.quote: 45 in NAMRA and about 4 odd crores in Arman. So 45 plus 4, about 50 odd crores. 50 odds, on that.

items.statement: Micro LAP pilot at 1% of AUM, currently in 15 branches in Gujarat with expansion to 25 branches planned, disbursement run rate ~Rs. 3 crores/month targeting Rs. 5-7 crores/month in coming quarters
items.quote: Overall in micro LAP. I think you'll get a better idea. So we had not disbursed till Q3. I know that. Q3 we have not. January and later we have started dispersing.

items.statement: MSME disbursement run rate currently ~Rs. 40 crores/month, expected to reach Rs. 60 crores/month by Q1 or Q3 FY26, but no branch expansion due to OPEX constraints
items.quote: I would have expected a sort of a disbursement run rate at this point of being at least around 50 to 60 crores. But clearly we are not there yet. We are at more around 40 crores or so. So let's say by first or 3nd Quarter we can read somewhere in the neighborhood of 60 odd crores of disbursement rate.

items.statement: CGFMU guarantee cover enrolled for ~Rs. 200 crores of Q3 disbursements, covering 72% of principal at ~1% annual premium plus GST
items.quote: as of quarter three disbursements, which let's say ab out Rs. 200 crores of disbursements that have taken place in quarter three, have a guarantee cover through the

items.statement: Microfinance rejection rates at 80-82% due to tightened underwriting with independent credit department at branch level
items.quote: Rejection rates are like 80%-82% right now, right? And that's not something to be proud of mean, very few lending businesses can run with that kind of rejection rates.

items.statement: Management expects to see bottom by March 2025 with improvement from Q1 FY26, but recovery will take several quarters
items.quote: I think my estimate which I gave one quarter ago remains the same, that we will see the bottom by March. Already I feel that we have probably reached the bottom, but I am refraining myself from that conclusion because I don't have the data available with me to call it yet.

items.statement: No top-offs, restructuring, net-offs, or ERC transactions done; all necessary provisions taken in current period, nothing pushed to FY26
items.quote: If your question is, can we pushing anything forward for FY26, the simple answer is no, absolutely not. So I think people who have known us in the past will attest that we have not done any top-offs, not done any restructuring, not done any net-off type things.

items.statement: Liquidity position strong with Rs. 262 crores in cash, liquid investments, undrawn CC limits plus Rs. 120 crores undrawn sanctions from existing lenders
items.quote: our liquidity position remains strong with cash and bank balances, liquid investments, and undrawn CC limits amounting to Rs. 262 crores. Additionally, we have Rs. 120 crores in undrawn sanctions from existing len ders, ensuring continued financial flexibility

items.statement: Namra Finance Q3 PAT loss of Rs. 17.2 crores due to Rs. 67 crores impairment cost; MSME PAT Rs. 9.9 crores
items.quote: The cautious lending approach along with aggressive provisioning has impacted short-term profitability with Namra's Q3 profit after taxes at a loss of Rs. 17.2 crores due to increased impairment cost of Rs. 67 crores this quarter.

items.statement: Stage 2 (30-90 DPD) provision cover at 42% ECL for Namra microfinance book

items.quote: Roughly around Rs. 150 crore approx further warrant is going to come. Certain amount of roughly around Rs. 26 crore from Vivad se Vishwas is also expected.

items.statement: Demand is strong and expected to continue growing in the coming future.
items.quote: The demand is pretty strong at this moment. And we foresee a good growth in the coming future.

items.statement: Management is confident of driving ADR growth and sees considerable upside in rates.
items.quote: We continue to drive ADR, and we're confident that we will be able to drive ADR like we've done in the past, and there's no reason for that to change.

items.statement: Hotels are underpriced relative to global peers, providing significant rate upside.
items.quote: We're still, in my view, underpriced for the quality of hotels that we offer, both in parts of Asia and in leisure and business, and also in Europe and North America.

items.statement: CapEx spent on London asset, Tirupati, Rajgarh, Gandikota, Hebbal, and renovations like Trident Nariman Point.
items.quote: We have invested roughly 241 crores in our London asset and also we have spent on CapEx. The few new hotels in the pipeline, which you see, we have spend around 200 crores.

items.statement: CapEx investments are happening in Tirupati, Rajgarh, and Gandikota projects.
items.quote: So, the spends are happening in Tirupati, Rajgarh and Gandikota projects. These 3 main places the investments are happening.

items.statement: Pipeline includes 19 properties: 13 hotels, 3 Trident hotels, 3 Luxury Boats & Nile Cruisers; 8 owned, 11 managed; 10 domestic, 9 international.
items.quote: Overall, if I look at the summary, we're going to add 13 hotels, 3 Trident hotels and will also add 3 Luxury Boats & Nile Cruiser. If we take the split, we are increasing in all geographies, including domestic and international - domestic growth of 10, and 9 international. Out of 19, owned are 8 and managed properties will be 11.

items.statement: Two new management contracts signed (one Oberoi, one Trident in India); press release next week.
items.quote: A press release will be coming out next week on two further management contracts that have been signed since our last presentation to you. Both of these hotels, one is a Oberoi, one is a Trident, and they both are in India.

items.statement: Oberoi Grand Kolkata expected to open in about 18 months.
items.quote: So, Oberoi Grand should open in about 18 months.

items.statement: Oberoi Rajgarh expected to start operations around August.
items.quote: So, hopefully in and around August.

items.statement: Flight services business saw significant margin improvement.
items.quote: It's been a significant improvement on margin as well.

items.statement: MICE and wedding segment remains very strong with high F&B spend and room rates.
items.quote: I continue to see the MICE being very strong for that segment, I continue to see parents are willing to make that event very special and memorable for their family.

items.statement: No correlation analysis done between stock market declines and hotel demand; recent market decline has not impacted RevPAR growth.
items.quote: We haven't done that analysis to correlate the stock market movements with our business. But what I can say which is reflected in the numbers is that we have strong RevPAR growth at high occupancy levels.

items.statement: Focus on driving ARR even at cost of occupancy to maximize RevPAR and bottom-line flow-through.
items.quote: Our focus will be to drive rates even at the cost of occupancy because you can by increasing rate the flow through to bottom line is 100% and that's going to continue to be our focus, to drive ARR.

items.statement: Company does not provide revenue guidance.
items.quote: We don't do guidance. Maybe we should but I don't know, Navin, and maybe we can have a chat separately but we've shied away from guidance.

items.statement: Actively seeking partner for an Oberoi hotel in Hyderabad.
items.quote: Absolutely, we'd love to have an Oberoi in Hyderabad. So, if anybody who's on the call is interested in partnering with us for a hotel in Hyderabad, we'd love that.

items.statement: Full year EBITDA fell 28% to INR1.5 billion and EBIT fell 36% to INR1.04 billion in CY24 due to raw material inflation, adverse mix, high freight costs and one-off items.
items.quote: Full year EBITDA stands at INR1.5 billion compared to INR2.1 billion in 2023, it reflects a decrease of almost 28%. And when we look at the EBIT for full year, it is INR1.04 billion versus INR1.6 billion we have in 2023, which also reflect a decrease of slightly higher than 28%, so that decrease is 36% in case of EBIT.

items.statement: Margin pressure stems from raw material inflation, unfavorable product mix, high freight costs from the Red Sea crisis, and one-off items including fair value impairment.
items.quote: The pressure on margin has arisen due to the cost inflation, which include raw material inflation, sales and unfavorable product mix, high freight costs due to Sea crisis and a couple of one-off items, one-off item we spoke in the first quarter in the March 2024 on fairly impairment and all.

items.statement: FMCG demand is under pressure from inflation across most segments, with heightened competition from small players impacting mix; rural demand shows improvement but urban recovery timing is uncertain.
items.quote: In the overall ecosystem FMCG sector from which HIL derives bulk of our demand, inflationary pressures are impacting demand across most of the segments, barring a few, and it's affecting consumer spending, and this is having a spiral impact.

items.statement: Rural economy shows promising improvement in consumption; urban demand is taking time to recover and timing is unknown.
items.quote: But other side, if you look at rural economy is showing some promising improvement. However, urban is taking time. So expectation is that when we read the articles and something is there really expected that urban is also going to come back. But when? We don't know yet.

items.statement: Blueloop sustainable packaging contribution rose from 25% to 27.5% of sales in CY24, but high-end complex structures that drive premium margins are still in early adoption.
items.quote: And as you rightly pointed out, we moved our blueloop contribution from -- sales contribution from 25% to 27% to 27.5% in last year.

items.statement: Blueloop contribution was around 22% in CY22 and 25% in CY23, rising a couple of percentage points each year; current structures are low-end with limited differentiation.
items.quote: So '23, it was around 25%. And '22, I think I remember around 22%. So it's like we have moved a couple of percent points every year.

items.statement: No major capex planned for CY25; only routine maintenance capex across 10 plants, unlike prior large investments for blueloop.
items.quote: But in 2025, we are not planning for any big capex per se. But obviously, when you have managing 10 plants and always there will be one another capex will be there. So we'll continue to focus on making sure that we are having our operations, which is running and we don't have any challenges.

items.statement: Capacity utilization has headroom of 15-20% more production with current capacity.
items.quote: But by and far, if you look at, I think we can do more production with the similar capacity. So we do have a room of somewhere between 15% to 20% more production.

items.statement: Geopolitical and tariff developments may create export opportunities for India, but also pose uncertainty; management sees India as a potential net gainer.
items.quote: But going forward, considering that what's happening as a tariff, I don't want to go any country-specific, but you know you are monitoring the market. There are definitely chances that India as a whole may emerge as a net gainer by whatever is tariff situation happening elsewhere in the globe.

items.quote: Point noted. And definitely, we, as a management also and we make sure that whatever the cost we had, and we ensure that there are a consumer benefit for that. And yes, point well noted. Thank you.

items.quote: But I can see that now the demand coming back strongly. Our end customers are also having some positive sentiment. So we shall see that in future quarters. We should see some revival.

items.quote: So in the light of this, I would say that considering the good performance of standalone in Q4, we should be doing about INR100 crores of EBITDA for the full year.

items.quote: At a standalone level, we should be able to achieve around 13% to 14%. And at a subsidiary level, including Canada, we should be between 6% to 7% of EBITDA.

items.quote: We expect to close the year with gross accounting 13% of revenue growth as against the 18%, and mainly because of the drop in the subsidiary.

items.statement: No FY26 consolidated guidance given pending Canadian subsidiary strategic decisions
items.quote: At this point of time, I wouldn't guide anything. Let us -- because we have certain actions to take in the Canadian subsidiary, perhaps we can see it in the next concall.

items.statement: Target to improve subsidiary margins to 7% in short term and 11-12% in subsequent years
items.quote: Our objective is to try to move that margin up to a 7% level or so in the short-term in the coming year, and then push it up further as growth comes in to 11% to 12% range in the subsequent years.

items.statement: Standalone BTS EBITDA margin 18-20%, EMS 11-13% on yearly basis; French engineering services at 4% but pulled down by Canadian losses
items.quote: BTS generally is about 18% to 20%, and EMS, it is between 11% to 13%. And that is what we are targeting and we are achieving on a yearly basis.

items.quote: Our order book position stands at INR1,675 crores as on 31st December, 2024.

items.statement: Strong pipeline for Build to Spec and EMS in standalone business; expecting substantial Q4 orders in radar/naval and missile programs
items.quote: In Q4, we are also expecting some substantial orders, and we will receive them from the radar domain, and these are for naval programs.

items.statement: Canadian subsidiary losses dragging consolidated P&L; strategic decisions on Canadian operations expected in next couple of quarters
items.quote: We will be basically making some strategic decisions with regard to the Canadian operations in the next couple of quarters to ensure that it doesn't continue to drag the overall P&L.

items.statement: Worst case Canadian subsidiary drag to stop by September; variation orders and knowledge transfer to India underway
items.quote: The worst case before September we should be able to ensure that Canada is no longer a dragger.

items.statement: Board approved fundraising via QIP or other means for growth capital; timing to be decided
items.quote: We sought and got approval from our Board to be able to raise some funds through either a QIP or other means.

items.quote: On the subsidiary front, obviously, it depends on what we will end up doing with the Canadian subsidiary and also in terms of the improvement on utilization in France, which we are doing.

items.statement: Domestic BTS business focused on defense/space (electronic warfare, space, radars, land systems); EMS adding strategic customers in ramp-up phase
items.quote: So with all of this, I think these are -- electronic warfare, space, radars and land systems are broadly areas that we have been building strong capabilities in.

items.statement: Negotiating variation orders with Canadian customers to cover engineering costs; shifting work from Canada to India for cost advantage
items.quote: First, in the short-term itself, we are -- we've been negotiating quite strongly with some of our customers to obtain additional purchase orders for -- or additional variation orders for the -- to support the engineering team in Canada.

items.quote: As a matter of abundant caution and prudence, we have provided for the entire exposure. But as it evolves, perhaps in the next month or so, we should be able to get a better clarity.

items.statement: EBITDA margins should improve from next financial year as annual procurement contracts expire on 31st March 2025
items.quote: See, the EBITDA margins should certainly improve going forward from coming year because our procurement contracts are for -- on an annual basis, which will expire by 31st of March this year.

items.quote: Top line growth, we are certainly looking, as I was telling earlier to replying to a question that we expect made me to grow much faster than what we have shown so far.

items.statement: Building Products segment will grow faster than current rates
items.quote: Building Products segment will grow faster than what we have grown so far. Thinking that the growth rates will be faster than what we have today.

items.statement: Agriculture segment to continue growing at 8% to 10% annual rate
items.quote: Agriculture will continue to grow as per the regular 8% to 10% annual growth rate.

items.statement: INR20 crores capex already spent in current year; expansion plans nearing finalization before end of financial year
items.quote: Already during this current year, INR20 crores capex has been -- payout has been already made, and we are further going ahead with our plans.

items.statement: Building Products segment EBITDA margins expected to gradually reach industry levels of 16% to 20%
items.quote: you will see generally industry is showing between 16% to 20% EBITDA margins. So we will try to catch up with the industry in EBITDA, but it takes -- it doesn't happen in steps.

items.statement: Raw material procurement contracts linked to Platt prices; local market prices 7-9% below contracted rates
items.quote: the difference between local market and the raw material manufacturers or landed prices were to the significant extent of 8%, 7%, 9% with month-to-month, they will be even higher than that.

items.statement: Building materials demand consistent across all regions; temporary rain impact of 10-15 days only
items.quote: as far as building materials are concerned, the demand is consistent and across all segments across India. It is not affected by sudden rains or short rain cycles.

items.statement: Government anti-dumping duty on PVC awaited; notification circulated but not yet announced
items.quote: Government has already issued and circulated country-wise manufacture-wise ADD, which they would like to apply. The only notification is awaited, which we are still not…

items.statement: Promoters converted INR17 crores warrants into equity; remaining 50% conversion in next financial year
items.quote: Only promoters have converted about 17 crores worth of warrants into equity. And the reason I always explain, you see in the current stock exchange rules, if you are having acquisition of more than 5% on a basis, it triggers certain other rules.

items.statement: Focus on Building Products and Agri segments; Industrial segment exposure to remain limited
items.quote: Our major focus will be BP, where we are growing well, and we are getting reasonably good response. And this is along with Agri that will be our major focus of business.

items.statement: Industrial segment sales down 73%; minimal outstanding receivables from institutional business
items.quote: we have come down from in institution by 73% sales are down. So you can understand hardly outstandings are there.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 may still be weak; significant improvement expected from Q1 FY26
items.quote: I think the things have started getting on a correction side. I would say that this Q4 may be still not that great. But from Q1 next year, we hope to be doing much better.

items.statement: SCD achieved 11.8% EBITDA margin in Q3 FY25, first time crossing double digits
items.quote: Particularly Suprajit Controls division had a good turnaround in this quarter. For the first time, it has declared a double-digit EBITDA margin of 12%, 11.8%.

items.statement: SCD margin improvement driven by operational excellence across plants except Matamoros
items.quote: Except Matamoros, all other pieces of the puzzle have been performing well compared to last year. I think that is why the margins have improved for the quarter.

items.statement: Chairman believes SCD double-digit margin is sustainable going forward
items.quote: Is it sustainable? I would believe so that it is sustainable. I think the operations continues to be pretty good going forward.

items.statement: SED installed new SMT production line now fully operational
items.quote: To cater to the growing needs of our customers, we also inst alled a new SMT production line, which is now fully operational and will help us fill capacity and manage capacity going forward

items.statement: SED margins impacted by product mix changes in EV 2-wheeler segment
items.quote: As you know, the EV market in India last quarter is quite tumultuous and there were quite a few changes in the volumes of many players. This meant that revenue grew, but some of the margins were impacted by product mix changes.

items.statement: Indian automotive growth below expectations with flat PV and moderate 2-wheeler growth
items.quote: We all know that it was not up to the expectations and there was a flat passenger vehicles and moderate 2-wheeler growth. Industry grew by around 10% for the 9 months as of December 2024.

items.statement: US market sentiment flat due to tariff uncertainty and ICE vs EV questions
items.quote: So, these are some of the h aunting questions in the auto industry and that has led to a flat sentiment in the U.S. market and also kept the industry on wait and watch

items.statement: Europe continues to flounder with political indecisiveness and production cuts
items.quote: Europe continues to flounder. It continues its political indecisiveness and lack of economic stability. We have all been hearing about huge manpower cuts at OEMs, production cuts, Tier 1s, economic brinkmanship at the smaller niche vendors.

items.statement: SCD winning new contracts across plants including electronic products for EV division
items.quote: U.S. team also continues to win great business like Europe. But what is very important is in the last quarter, we saw them winning business for the electronic products, at least for our electric EV division, like various sensors, starters from 2 of the major off-highway OEMs.

items.statement: SAL Automotive won significant new contracts ramping up in coming quarters
items.quote: Suprajit Automotive has been winning some significant, significant large contracts, and you will see in the upcoming quarters, the growth of SAL Automotive will be even more exciting as we have won multiple new contracts, which will all go into production in the next few quarters starting now.

items.statement: Matamoros faces tariff and labor cost challenges; legal case progressing slowly
