items.statement: In-sourcing electronics boards and motors from India to reduce Matamoros costs
items.quote: We are in the process of getting that particular product also in the process of being approved with customers. So once it is done, I think we will have a two-pronged cost reduction happening in that project, which would be a significant saving going forward.

items.statement: Morocco plant moving from 3-shift to 1-shift operation showing productivity gains
items.quote: We have, for example, moved from a 3-shift operation, we are moving to just about a 1-shift operation, which shows the kind of productivity improvements that we could have done on the same revenue and sales.

items.statement: SCS Europe turnaround expected in next few quarters; China/Canada profitable from April
items.quote: From 1st of April onwards, I think the numbers should look slightly better. And of course, the work in SCS Europe, it continues for at least 2 to 3 quarters.

items.statement: Indian cable exports grew 35% in 9 months ended Dec 2024
items.quote: Our Indian cable exports saw a fantastic 35% growth. This shows the underlying strength in our global strategy as to how we have moved literally almost, I would say, conquered the Western world.

items.statement: SMT line captive use expected to improve EBITDA by 1% to 2% over time
items.quote: But over a period of time, we expect at least 1% to 2% improvement in EBITDA through these initiatives for the internal consumption, captive consumption.

items.statement: IATF certification for automotive EMS expected in a couple of quarters max
items.quote: Work on that is going on, and we should be certified in a couple of quarters max because that needs some kind of preparation.

items.statement: Products and Solutions addressable market growing at 8% to 10%
items.quote: My understanding is the market is growing at about 8 to 10 percent.

items.statement: Solar O&M megawatts under management expected to reach 800 to 900 by year end
items.quote: I think we hope to end the year with about 800 to 900 megawatts under management, and it will consistently grow on that side.

items.statement: EMS expansion timeline depends on business growth and ODM partner investment decisions
items.quote: If the business grows really fast, those number of lines can come fast. If the business does not come in, those lines in 3 years also will not make any meaning.

items.statement: Mobile printers gaining traction in government and BFSI segments
items.quote: That is where the traction is, because if you notice the Department of Post was one big customer, a couple of others who are looking at taking the print or the business to the last mile into much more of the heart of India, that is where the mobile printers are being used and commissioned and that is where the use case has increased.

items.statement: Company investing 2% to 3% of revenue in EMS and R&D growth initiatives
items.quote: as explained in the earlier calls, we are continuing to invest 2% to 3% of our revenue in growth initiatives like EMS and R&D

items.statement: Retail sector growth has been very slow and a dampener
items.quote: the retail sector has been very, very, the growth has been very slow, and it has been quite a dampener as regards to that.

items.statement: Additional SMT lines will be added as EMS business grows
items.quote: as and when the growth happens, the additional lines will come. At this point of time, I think it is purely subject to the growth of the business and as the business grows, I think we should be in a position to add the lines as required.

items.statement: No specific timeline given for breaking even at EBT level
items.quote: However, we expect like in the future, this investment of 2% to 3% expected to contribute for growth much bigger than what we are growing 15% and expected to result in a positive margin at the bottom line.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM target 22,000-23,000 crore by FY25 end, yield normalization next financial year
items.quote: I think the year we should end at around 22, 23 and it will take maybe some more time to get to 25.

items.statement: Gold loan yield recovery of at least 1% in Q1 FY26, full normalization next financial year
items.quote: I expect at least 1% to be recovered in the first quarter of the new fiscal year itself. But it's very difficult to be precise on the forecast.

items.statement: MFI credit cost guidance 8-8.5% for current period
items.quote: On an average, we will be looking at a credit cost of around, for this, around 8% to 8.5% kind of a thing.

items.statement: MFI asset quality bottoming out now, worst quarter was Q3 FY25
items.quote: I think that we should be bottoming out now.

items.statement: Worst is behind us, things should improve from Q4 FY25
items.quote: I believe that we have taken, in case of MSME, our insurance cover starts from the loans, I think from September or October. In microfinance, I think some pain is still there, but it may not be as bad as the third quarter, which was the worst ever quarter.

items.statement: Raised INR 9,964 crore through term loans, bonds, CP and INR 1,477 crore from assignment in Q3 FY25
items.quote: During the quarter, we raised INR 9,964 crores through term loans, bonds, and commercial paper and INR 1,477 crores was raised from assignment.

items.statement: Gold loan portfolio yield down ~2% due to competitive customer acquisition
items.quote: Gold loan volume growth is there, but the portfolio yield is down by almost 2%.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing increased 9 bps YoY and 1 bps QoQ to 9.16%
items.quote: Our quarterly average cost of borrowing increased 9 basis points year-on-year and 1 basis point quarter-on-quarter to hit 9.16%.

items.statement: Gold loan volume growing strongly, reached 15,000 crore from 10,000 at ban
items.quote: At the time of ban, we had 10,000, then we went up to 11,000 in the 10 days after the ban in September then 15,000.

items.statement: Karnataka MFI ordinance causing slight disturbances despite exemption for regulated entities
items.quote: We expect slight disturbances for a couple of months or so till people -- I mean, even now if you look at it on the ground, most of the stakeholders have understood that it is not for the regulated entities and things, but slight disturbances will affect K arnataka for slightly little thing

items.statement: Liquidity buffer INR 5,656 crore as of Dec 31, covers 6 months maturities of INR 5,297 crore
items.quote: Our cash and cash equivalent and committed credit lines from banks and institutions stood at INR5,656 crores. This is adequate to meet near-term liabilities, but also fund growth.

items.statement: Dollar bond raised in Jan 2025 at near double-digit cost, will impact Q4 FY25 cost of funds
items.quote: The dollar bond that we have raised in the month of January with full hedging, the cost is significantly higher. It's almost kind of double digit, and that will impact the weighted average cost of fund going forward.

items.statement: Capital adequacy dipped to 22% from 26.3% QoQ due to loan growth and lower assignments, expected to recover as assignments pick up
items.quote: So the capital adequacy margin is down because the loan book has grown, Mr. Lee. And as I said that the assignments have been much lower because they require seasoning.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 15-20% for FY26 and EBITDA margin guidance of 14.5-15% for FY26
items.quote: anywhere close to between 15% to 20% would be our estimate in terms of the top line growth. I think our endeavour is to continue to sustain and further expand these EBITDA margins in FY '26 as well.

items.statement: Full year FY25 consolidated revenue expected around INR 3,500 crores with similar EBITDA margin in Q4
items.quote: we should be looking – to similar a 9 -monthFY25 growth, anywhere between 20% to 25%, which should ideally get the total consolidated revenues closer to around INR 3,500 crores, and we should be able to sustain a similar EBITDA margin in quarter 4 as well.

items.statement: Capex guidance for full year FY25 remains INR 130-140 crores; INR 83 crores spent in 9 months
items.quote: The capex outlay during 9 months has been at INR83 crores, majorly on account of new products SOPs in IAC and Lumax Alps. The guidance for the full year remains at INR 130 crores to INR140 crores.

items.statement: Total order book INR 1,350 crores with 90% new business; 30% maturing in FY26, 40% in FY27, 30% in FY28; EV contribution ~40%
items.quote: The total order book, considering the value of all product categories, are INR 1,350 crores, out of which 90% is new business. 30% order book value will mature in FY '26, 40% in FY '27 and remaining 30% in FY '28. EV contribution is approximately 40% of the total order book.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 14% for Q3 and 9M FY25; FY26 guidance 14.5-15%; levers are JV turnaround and Aftermarket recovery
items.quote: I think my margin guidance would be that anywhere close to 14.5% to 15% which we should be looking at perhaps in FY '26 at a consolidated level. We are having a significant presence of the order book coming into the next year itself, backed by multiple small joint ventures, which are firing. Aftermarket also for FY '26, we do expect the double-digit growth to bounce back, which is operating at a h

items.statement: Raw material pricing showing signs of increase but recoverable from OEMs in 3-6 months
items.quote: There are certain signs of raw material pricing going up. But again, that is a lag. We should be able to recover them from the OEMs in 3 to 6 months' time frame.

items.statement: PV growth muted at 3-5% in FY26; 2W to surpass FY19 peak of 24.5M units with low double-digit growth; CV recovery expected in FY26 with govt/private capex uptick
items.quote: The 2-wheeler industry, however, will continue to outperform the other segments, even in the current year, as I mentioned, the 2-wheeler industry has reported a double-digit growth, and we are fairly certain that in FY '26, we will surpass the FY '19 historic production volume of about 24.5 million units.

items.statement: PV share increased to 50% in 9M FY25 from 47% last year; 2/3W at 25%, Aftermarket 12%, CV 8%
items.quote: With increased focus on passenger vehicle segment and integration of IAC, our share of passenger vehicle stood at 50% in 9 months FY '25 as compared to 47% in last year.

items.statement: Tata Motors EV program delayed by ~6 months due to design revamp after Mahindra BEV launches; initial revenue expectation INR 30-35 crores
items.quote: We expect the delay to be about 6 months. And this delay is primarily driven by one single factor, which is the recent launch of Mahindra BEVs, which are in the market, has created a l ot of momentum in the EV market.

items.statement: OBD2 norms implementation from 1 Apr 2025 to add INR 60-70 crores revenue to Lumax FAE in FY26; increases 2W content per vehicle by ~INR 800
items.quote: We are anticipating almost INR 60 crores to INR70 crores increase in our top line revenues with the implementation of the secondary oxygen sensor, which now becomes mandatory from 1st April 2025.

items.statement: Mechatronics segment grew 75% in 9M FY25; order book INR 320 crores; expect to almost double revenue in FY26 with margins at or above consolidated level
items.quote: I think overall, my commentary would be that we've seen a significant growth in the Mechatronics vertical. And for the next year onwards, we do expect to almost double our revenue within the Mechatronics vertical.

items.statement: IAC India 9M revenue INR 800 crores, up 20% YoY; order book INR 500-550 crores; FY26 manufacturing growth expected 15%+ on full year EV launch realization
items.quote: IAC total revenue for 9 months of this fiscal stood at INR 800 crores. And again, maybe I'll request Sunil Koparkar to just take the question on Tata Motors launch date and value of the business for IAC.

items.statement: Aftermarket Q4 FY25 expected double-digit growth vs Q4 FY24; target to double revenue in 3 years driven by exports
items.quote: for quarter 4 stand alone, we should be looking at a good double-digit growth rate, which is pretty similar to what the Aftermarket division used to do up until FY '24. Giving you a horizon, I think this growth momentum in FY '26 will continue very healthy into a double-digit territory. And yes, our endeavor is still to double the Aftermarket revenues in the next 3-year time frame, given the fact

items.statement: Greenfuel CNG kit content per vehicle currently INR 4,000; expected to increase to INR 8,000-10,000 in FY26; export potential in Africa with 2,000 kits already supplied
items.quote: as of now, in P&L, there is a content per vehicle of INR4,000 on account of CNG. But going forward in next year, we are seeing that content to increase to somewhere closer to INR 8,000 to INR 10,000 per vehicle.

items.statement: Lumax Cornaglia grew 5% in 9M despite anchor customer volumes down 5%; new SOPs for rooftops of E3-wheelers and body cabins in next 2 months
items.quote: Lumax Cornaglia, in spite of its anchor customer being down this year in production volumes by 5%, still reported about 5% kind of a top line increase.

name: Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Ltd

items.statement: Demerger of western wear brands into ABLBL set for completion within next 2-3 months; NCLT hearing scheduled third week of March 2025
items.quote: First, the demerger of western wear brands business into a separate entity, that is Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited, or ABLBL, is progressing well and set for completion within the next 2, 3 months. The NCLT hearing is scheduled in third week of March 2025.

items.statement: Secured USD 490 million equity capital via QIP and preferential issue; will make demerged ABFRL debt-free with cash for growth until self-sustainable
items.quote: Number two, the company has successfully secured USD 490 mil lion equity capital through a mix of QIP and preferential issue. The fundraise within demerged ABFRL will strengthen its Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited (ABFRL) February 17, 2025 balance sheet by making it debt -free and leaving enough cash in the books to take care of the growth needs of its businesses until they become self-sus

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded to 15.9% in Q3 FY25 from 14.5% in Q3 FY24; YTD margin 13.2% vs 12.5%
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA stood at INR683 crores, growing 13% Y -o-Y in absolute terms, with 15.9% margin as against 14.5% margin in Q3 last year.

items.statement: ABLBL EBITDA margin 16.5% in Q3 FY25, up 90 bps YoY; Brands margin 19.6%
items.quote: ABLBL posted revenue of INR2,151 crores with EBITDA of INR355 crores in Q3 FY '25 and an EBITDA margin of 16.5%, 90 basis point expansion versus last year.

items.statement: Demerged ABFRL EBITDA margin 14.4% in Q3 FY25, up 250 bps from 11.9%
items.quote: The proposed demerged ABFRL reported a 3% Y -o-Y revenue growth, reaching INR2,218 crores. EBITDA stood at INR320 crores with an EBITDA margin of 14.4%, marking an increase of 250 basis points from 11.9% in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Pantaloons EBITDA margin 19.3% in Q3 FY25, up over 170 bps YoY
items.quote: On profitability front, the segment reported an EBITDA margin of 19.3%, reflecting an improvement of over 170 basis points Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Ethnic portfolio EBITDA margin 19.2% in Q3 FY25, up 1,160 bps YoY
items.quote: Profitability for the overall portfolio also improved sharply with EBITDA margins reaching 19.2%, a remarkable 1,160 basis point Y-o-Y expansion.

items.statement: Overall consumption remains subdued with inconsistent footfalls outside festive/wedding season; Lifestyle Brands retail LTL grew 12% driven by strong festive/wedding performance
items.quote: The overall consumption remains subdued this quarter as well with periods of high to moderate consumption. While the festive and wedding season witnessed robust demand, other periods experienced inconsistent footfalls.

items.statement: Lifestyle Brands retail LTL growth of 12% across brands on 2,500+ stores; momentum expected to continue
items.quote: Lifestyle Brands, the brands have seen a retail LTL growth of 12% across brands on a network of more than 2,500 stores.

items.statement: Lifestyle Brands strategically optimizing network and channels to enhance distribution quality; exiting underperforming markets and restructuring wholesale/e-comm partnerships
items.quote: Over the past few quarters, in context of the market situation, brands have taken the opportunity to strategically optimize their network and channels to enhance overall quality of its distribution. This involved exiting underpe rforming markets and formats and restructuring business arrangements with wholesale and e -commerce partners to drive profitability.

items.statement: ABLBL plans aggressive expansion with 300+ new stores over next 12 months across portfolio
items.quote: Over the next 12 months, the brands are poised for an aggressive expansion with a significant rollout of 300 -plus new stores across the portfolio.

items.statement: Pantaloons opened 13-15 stores in FY25, closed ~20; plans 15-20 new stores in FY26 with ongoing network refinement
items.quote: specifically for this year, I think by the end of the financial year, we would have opened about 13 to 15 stores. We have a few more to go in the next few weeks before the end of the financial year. And just this year alone, we would have shut about 20-odd stores. We have shut a few and a few are about to

items.statement: Style Up to end FY25 with 48-50 stores; plans to add ~50 stores in FY26 (minimum doubling)
items.quote: We expect this year to end with a network between 45 to 50 stores -- 48 to 50 stores. Next year, we'll definitely, at the minimum level, double it. As we go along during the course of the year, we'll see if we can expand faster than that. But at this point, I think the number that I would play out is about 50 more stores next year.

items.statement: Tasva at ~70 stores currently; plans to add 40-50 stores in FY26
items.quote: I think it would be in the range of 40 to 50 stores from the current level of about -- we end this year at about 70-odd stores, and we should be able to probably add closer to 50 stores next year.

items.statement: Phasing out F21 offline operations; accelerated store closures in Q4 FY25; online F21 remains subscale
items.quote: As you may be already aware, the company is in the process of phasing out its F21 offline operations, which has had a moderate impact on the growth of the emerging segment and also impacted its overall profitability.

items.statement: Management says FY25 revenue will not reach Rs 2,000 crore target due to weak institutional sales and poor southern crop season
items.quote: We will not be able to touch 2,000 crores, but yes, considering the profitability and all, cost margins and all those and working capital on, those parameters will be improving

items.statement: Management expects FY26 performance to be much better across all parameters with lower OPEX, full potential of patented products, and reduced inventory
items.quote: next year revenue would be for all the products with respect to full potential pl us with current cost optimization what we are making will have a much lower OPEX

items.statement: Q3 FY25 gross margin improved to 32% from 23% YoY due to higher branded sales share
items.quote: There was significant improvement in the gross margins from 23% in Q3 FY'24 to 32% in Q3 FY'25 due to higher sales of branded products

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA ex-other income was negative Rs 6 crore; reported loss of Rs 24 crore including Rs 11 crore forex loss
items.quote: Our Q3 FY '25 EBITDA, excluding other income, was around negative 6 crores and we reported a loss of Rs. 24 crores for this quarter

items.statement: Product prices reduced ~20% YoY due to China dumping and aggressive competition
items.quote: Further, there was around 20% reduction in the product prices

items.statement: Unseasonal rains and 35% drop in chilli prices caused farmer cash crunch, reducing crop protection spending in South India
items.quote: Chilli prices have dropped by around 35% from an average of around Rs. 19,000 per quintal in January 2024 to around Rs. 10,000 to Rs. 12,000 this year

items.statement: Branded business grew 50-70% YoY; institutional business consciously reduced by ~Rs 72 crore in Q3
items.quote: There was an increase in branded business by way of new product introduction and a volume growth from the existing products. This growth was compensated by r eduction in the institutional business by around Rs. 72 crores

items.statement: Targeting 65-70% branded / 30-40% B2B mix for FY26; patented products to reach 40-50% of branded sales
items.quote: We should be anywhere between 40 to 50% of our overall branded business coming from our patented products

items.statement: Preferential issue of Rs 150 crore: 25% received, 50 crore for capex, 100 crore for working capital; no fund utilization deviation
items.quote: earlier for 200 crores, we had mentioned that 70 crores will go for CAPEX. But now for 150, we hav e mentioned that 50 crores will go for CAPEX and balance 100 crores will go for working capital

items.statement: Capex allocation reduced to Rs 50 crore from Rs 70 crore in revised preferential issue of Rs 150 crore
items.quote: now for 150, we hav e mentioned that 50 crores will go for CAPEX and balance 100 crores will go for working capital

items.statement: Foreign currency payables of ~Rs 400 crore caused Rs 11 crore forex loss in December due to USD-INR spike
items.quote: We have close to 400 crores worth of foreign currency payable which we have to do

items.statement: Income tax issue from Sept 2023 believed closed with no notices since; no formal closure letter yet
items.quote: whatever we had issue last year, later on there was no notices and no responses, anything from the income tax side and what we believe is and what we understand from the department as well that the issue is closed from there

items.statement: 9-month operating cash flow positive Rs 175 crore; Q3 operating cash flow Rs 32 crore; inventory down to Rs 700 crore
items.quote: Cash flow from operations for 9 months was positive Rs. 175 crores and from this quarter it was around Rs. 32 crores

items.statement: NIM rose for three consecutive quarters to 8.7% in Q3 FY25 from 8.2% in Q2 FY25 and 6.7% in Q3 FY24
items.quote: our net interest margin which was a pain point for us in fiscal 23 and 24 has now risen for three consecutive quarters to 8.7% versus 8.2% in September 2024, and 6.7% in December 2023.

items.statement: Non-gold loan growth will be driven by secured green energy financing; unsecured MSME disbursements will continue to decline
items.quote: Going forward , majority of the growth in non -gold loans will be driven by secured green energy financing, with disbursements in the unsecured MSME portfolio continuing to decline, as we have seen in the last few quarters .

items.statement: Tighter liquidity in the NBFC sector and a cautious credit environment led to slower growth and lower disbursements
items.quote: the decline was due to a more selective credit approach, coupled with tighter liquidity in the NBFC sector

items.statement: Gross NPAs at 2.8% vs 2.6% in Q2 FY25; absolute gross NPAs up only 2.2% but percentage rose due to AUM decline
items.quote: Gross NPAs on the entire book stood at 2.8% versus 2.6% in September 2024. Please note that on an absolute basis, gross NPAs went up only 2.2% but on a percentage basis, gross NPAs are higher because the AUM has declined from 12 .2 billion to 11 .5 billion in the quarter.

items.statement: Slippages fell to 83 million from 162 million in Q2 FY25; recoveries rose to 76 million from 12 million
items.quote: Total slippages in the quarter were 83 million versus 162 million in September 2024 while recoveries in the quarter stood at 76 million versus 12 million in September 24.

items.statement: Board deliberated on strategic initiatives including equity raising; definitive disclosure expected by end of January 2025 via exchange filing
items.quote: the Board deliberated on the options that were put in front of the Board. So, we're very hopeful that by the end of this month, there will be something definitive that we can disclose to all investors through an exchange filing.

items.statement: Branch consolidation in Madhya Pradesh and Delhi (3-4 branches) to improve AUM per branch and profitability
items.quote: there's been some amount of consolidation with the branches just so that the AUM per branch would go up, and the profitability of the branch could be reached in much better fashion. This consolidation has happened largely in two geographies, which is in Madhya Pradesh and in Delhi, where three to four branches have been consolidated .

items.statement: Corporate agency license applied for; awaiting regulatory response
items.quote: the license which you are asking is corporate agency license and we have applied for that. We are waiting for their reply and accordingly we will let everyone know, but right now we have just applied for the corporate agency licence.

items.statement: Fees and commission income will remain subdued as BC relationship with Shivalik Small Finance Bank on gold loans was stopped in August due to RBI guidelines requiring gold to be kept with partner bank
items.quote: we had a BC relationship with Shivalik Small Finance Bank in the gold loan product. Unfortunately, from August that relationship we have to stop business given the fact that with the RBI guidelines in a BC relationship on gold loan, the gold had to be kept with the partner who is contributing the capital, which is the bank.

items.statement: Debt maturities: ~210-212 crores in FY26 and ~140 crores in FY27
items.quote: it's about 210 or 212 crores which is in fiscal 26 and fiscal 27 is about 140 odd crores.

items.statement: Repo rate cut of 25 bps has not yet percolated to cost of funds for smaller NBFCs lending to MSMEs
items.quote: For us there has been no impact on the repo rate decline so far, I think the macro environment right now at least for lenders who are lending to the MSME space or smaller NBFCs, I don't think much has percolated down to us or to some of the others, in terms of the decline of 25 basis points on the repo rate.

items.statement: FY25 revenue target around INR300 crores
items.quote: Yes, FY25 will be closing around 300.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target around INR400 crores
items.quote: Yes, 26 will be doing 400.

items.statement: Target INR500 crores revenue in next three years and INR1,000 crores in next five years
items.quote: Our target is to achieve INR500 crores revenue in the next three years, and INR1,000 crores in the next five years, driven by rising market demand and strategic growth initiatives.

items.statement: Net profit post-tax target of 5%
items.quote: Our target is net profit post-tax is 5%.

items.statement: Current expansion capex of INR60 crores (INR30 crores civil, INR30 crores machinery)
items.quote: Approximately, the capex into the civil which is the land, building and machinery, we have spent it around INR30 crores and in machinery around another INR30 crores.

items.statement: Future capex of roughly INR150 crores for INR1,000 crores revenue target
items.quote: We will be requiring a capex -- this land, building and machinery would be roughly INR150 crores.

items.statement: Current order book approximately INR130 crores (INR40-45 crores global, rest domestic)
items.quote: Order book, currently, if you see, we are having INR130 crores approximately orders. Out of INR130 crores, INR40 crores, INR45 crores are from the global market and rest are from the

items.statement: PAT margin improved 130 bps to 3.14% in Q3 FY25
items.quote: The PA T came in at INR3.14 crores, reflecting a remarkable year -on-year growth of 222.83%, with the PA T margin improving by 130 basis points to 3.14

items.statement: Revenue mix: ~50% sweaters, 30% jackets/outerwear, 20% t-shirts and shoe uppers
items.quote: Approximately 50% revenue is comi ng from sweaters, 30% from jackets, outerwear jackets and 20% balance from t-shirts as well as the shoes for business

items.statement: 15-month visibility from concept to delivery; orders already booked for new capacity
items.quote: We have already booked the orders for the new capacity to come. As I explained, this process is 15 months from concept to delivery. So, we have all the visibilities in which month what we have to do.

items.statement: Export target 50% of revenue (currently 25% exports, 75% domestic)
items.quote: We are focusing more on export business because we will increase this export percentage and our ultimate target is 50-50; 50% domestic and 50% global business.

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle 200-220 days (90-120 days credit + 90-120 days manufacturing)
items.quote: The total cycle is about 200 to 220 days because 90 to 120 days we require, give the credit to the brand and 90 to 120 days depending on the product is the manufacturing cycle.

items.statement: Capacity increasing ~70% with 150,000 sq ft expansion; peak revenue INR500 crores post-expansion
items.quote: We are doing approximately 70% increase on capacity.

items.statement: Funded expansion with internal accruals and INR32 crores bank debt out of INR60 crores total capex
items.quote: Against INR60 crores we have taken a debt of INR32 crores.

items.quote: Yes. We have already commissioned last mont h a solar power plant which is 15 % of my current contract demand from the

items.statement: FY25 revenue guided at INR650-670 crores
items.quote: FY '25, INR650 crores, INR670 crores, somewhere in that range we will be ending up.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guided at INR950-1000 crores with EBITDA margin 17-19%
items.quote: We are expecting revenue in the range of about INR950 crores to INR1,000 crores for FY '26. At the minimum EBITDA range between 17% to 19%.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guided at INR1250-1300 crores with EBITDA margin ~18%
items.quote: In FY '26, INR1,000 FY '27, which we assume that we will be running both the plant right from day 1 on a full capacity should be in the range of about INR1,250 crores to INR1,300 crores, again, EBITDA margin in the range of about 18% plus/minus one.

items.statement: INR125 crore fundraise: INR50 crore for debt repayment, INR75 crore retained for working capital and future expansion in FY25-26
items.quote: From this INR125 crores, INR50 crores, we are repaying the debt and balance we are going to retain with us for the use of future expansion work.

items.statement: Pakhajan facility full monetization needs 3-4 years due to INR250 crore peripheral infrastructure spend
items.quote: Well, Pakhajan is not fully monetized. It will take at least to monetize the full assets of Pakhajan, we will need 3 years minimum 3 to 4 years purely because we have spent about INR250 crores on peripheral infrastructure creation.

items.statement: Customer RFQs delayed to mid-2025; some approvals pending for key customers
items.quote: Customer RFQ coming, see customer has major customer runs on a yearly or 2 year contract. And that they should raise the RFQ for the new purchase. So that will be going to come somewhere in July, August.

items.statement: Sustainable gross margin guided at 38-39%
items.quote: I think gross margin of about 38% to 39% is a sustainable margin.

items.statement: Company-level EBITDA margin expected at ~18% (+/-1%) at full utilization
items.quote: I will not going to have a plant-wise EBITDA, but I can tell you on the company level, EBITDA will be plus/minus 1% of 18%.

items.statement: Chemical prices stabilized; expect consistent pricing for next few months; price improvements seen from mid-January
items.quote: Looking ahead, we understand that chemical prices have stabilized and expect to see consistent pricing for the next few months.

items.statement: Q4 volume growth guided at 30-35% aggregate by year-end
items.quote: Current quarter we should be having a volume growth, aggregate growth of about 30%, 35% by end of the year as an aggregate growth.

items.statement: Consumer chemical growth in Q3 was one-time due to subdued industrial sales and year-end customer closures
items.quote: No, it will be onetime. We don't expect that to grow this. This is purely that our sales into the industrial segment were a little subdued due to the demand and also the year-end for a lot of customers.

items.statement: Tariff impact uncertain; 10% China tariff expected to remain; India not expected to be heavily penalized
